title: An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae
authors: Jenner E
summary: Described cowpox inoculation protecting against smallpox, founding vaccination.

title: Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden
authors: Mendel G
venue: Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn 4:3-47
summary: Pea-hybrid crossing experiments establishing that discrete hereditary factors segregate and assort independently, founding genetics.

title: Ueber die chemische Zusammensetzung der Eiterzellen
authors: Miescher F
summary: Isolated a phosphorus-rich, non-protein substance from leucocyte nuclei that he called nuclein, the first description of DNA as a chemical entity.

title: Compte rendu sommaire des expériences faites à Pouilly-le-Fort, près de Melun, sur la vaccination charbonneuse
authors: Pasteur L, Chamberland C, Roux E
venue: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences 92
summary: Public demonstration of an attenuated anthrax vaccine in sheep, generalizing vaccination to laboratory-attenuated pathogens.

title: Ueber das Zustandekommen der Diphtherie-Immunität und der Tetanus-Immunität bei Thieren
authors: Behring E, Kitasato S
summary: Showed that serum from immunized animals transfers protection against diphtheria and tetanus toxins, founding antitoxin serum therapy and the concept of antibodies as therapeutics.

title: The treatment of malignant tumors by repeated inoculations of erysipelas: with a report of ten original cases
authors: Coley WB
venue: American Journal of the Medical Sciences 105:487–511
summary: Bacterial toxin injections ('Coley's toxins') induced tumor regressions, the earliest systematic cancer immunotherapy.

title: Animal Intelligence: An Experimental Study of the Associative Processes in Animals
authors: Thorndike EL
summary: Puzzle-box experiments with cats that led to the 'law of effect': actions followed by satisfying outcomes become more likely. This is the psychological root of trial-and-error reinforcement learning.

title: The chromosomes in heredity
authors: Sutton WS
summary: Proposed that Mendelian hereditary factors reside on chromosomes, uniting cytology with genetics in the chromosome theory of inheritance.

title: Sex limited inheritance in Drosophila
authors: Morgan TH
summary: The white-eye mutant linked a specific trait to the X chromosome, giving the first direct experimental evidence that genes lie on chromosomes.

title: Die Kinetik der Invertinwirkung
authors: Michaelis L, Menten ML
summary: Derived the Michaelis-Menten rate law for enzyme kinetics, the foundational quantitative model of biochemistry.

title: The reflection of X-rays by crystals
authors: Bragg WH, Bragg WL
summary: Established Bragg's law and X-ray crystal structure analysis, the origin of crystallography as a tool for atomic structure.

title: The internal secretion of the pancreas
authors: Banting FG, Best CH
venue: Journal of Laboratory and Clinical Medicine 7:251–266
summary: Isolation of pancreatic extracts (insulin) that lowered blood glucose in diabetic dogs, leading to the first protein hormone therapy.

title: Artificial transmutation of the gene
authors: Muller HJ
summary: Showed X-rays greatly increase mutation rate in Drosophila, proving genes are physical structures that can be altered experimentally.

title: The significance of pneumococcal types
authors: Griffith F
summary: Discovered bacterial transformation: heat-killed virulent pneumococci conferred their type on live avirulent cells, implying a transmissible 'transforming principle'.

title: Genetic control of biochemical reactions in Neurospora
authors: Beadle GW, Tatum EL
summary: Nutritional mutants of Neurospora established the one gene–one enzyme hypothesis, tying genes directly to specific biochemical steps.

title: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
authors: McCulloch WS, Pitts W
summary: Modeled neurons as binary threshold logic units and showed networks of them can compute logical functions, founding the theory of artificial neural networks.

title: Diagnosis of Uterine Cancer by the Vaginal Smear
authors: Papanicolaou GN, Traut HF
summary: Established the Pap smear for cytological cancer screening, which greatly reduced cervical cancer mortality.

title: Studies on the chemical nature of the substance inducing transformation of pneumococcal types
authors: Avery OT, MacLeod CM, McCarty M
summary: Purified Griffith's transforming principle and identified it as DNA, the first strong evidence that DNA is the hereditary material.

title: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
authors: Wiener N
summary: Founded cybernetics, framing feedback, control and information processing as common principles of animals and machines and shaping early neural-network research.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
authors: Shannon CE
summary: Founded information theory and introduced n-gram (Markov) approximations of English text, the conceptual ancestor of statistical language modeling.

title: The Organization of Behavior: A Neuropsychological Theory
authors: Hebb DO
summary: Proposed that synapses strengthen when pre- and post-synaptic neurons fire together (Hebbian learning), the first influential learning rule for neural networks.

title: Cultivation of the Lansing strain of poliomyelitis virus in cultures of various human embryonic tissues
authors: Enders JF, Weller TH, Robbins FC
summary: Grew poliovirus in non-neural tissue culture, enabling mass production of viral vaccines (Nobel 1954).

title: Chemical specificity of nucleic acids and mechanism of their enzymatic degradation
authors: Chargaff E
summary: Established that in DNA adenine equals thymine and guanine equals cytosine while base composition varies between species, the key constraint behind base pairing.

title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
authors: Turing AM
summary: Proposed the imitation game (Turing test), framing machine intelligence in terms of natural-language conversation.

title: The structure of proteins: two hydrogen-bonded helical configurations of the polypeptide chain
authors: Pauling L, Corey RB, Branson HR
summary: Predicted the alpha-helix from stereochemical principles, founding the idea of regular protein secondary structure.

title: A Stochastic Approximation Method
authors: Robbins H, Monro S
summary: Introduced stochastic approximation, the mathematical basis of stochastic gradient descent used to train virtually all neural networks.

title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
authors: Hodgkin AL, Huxley AF
summary: Coupled differential equations reproducing the action potential from measured ionic conductances, the archetype of mechanistic biological modeling (Nobel 1963).

title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis
authors: Turing AM
venue: Phil Trans R Soc Lond B 237(641):37-72
summary: Showed reaction-diffusion systems can spontaneously form patterns, founding mathematical theories of developmental pattern formation.

title: Independent functions of viral protein and nucleic acid in growth of bacteriophage
authors: Hershey AD, Chase M
summary: Radioisotope labelling of phage showed DNA, not protein, enters the host and carries genetic information, settling the question Avery had opened.

title: Molecular configuration in sodium thymonucleate
authors: Franklin R, Gosling RG
summary: X-ray fibre diffraction of B-form DNA (including Photo 51) giving the helical parameters and phosphate-outside geometry that constrained the double helix.

title: Molecular structure of nucleic acids: a structure for deoxyribose nucleic acid
authors: Watson JD, Crick FHC
summary: The antiparallel double helix with complementary A-T and G-C base pairs, immediately suggesting a copying mechanism for heredity.

title: Studies in human subjects on active immunization against poliomyelitis. I. A preliminary report of experiments in progress
authors: Salk JE
summary: First human results with formalin-inactivated poliovirus vaccine, leading to the 1954 field trial and 1955 licensure.

title: Distributional Structure
authors: Harris ZS
summary: Articulated the distributional hypothesis that words occurring in similar contexts have similar meanings, the basis of later vector semantics.

title: Enzymatic synthesis of deoxyribonucleic acid
authors: Kornberg A, Lehman IR, Bessman MJ, Simms ES
summary: First template-dependent enzymatic synthesis of DNA in vitro, the discovery of DNA polymerase and the start of in vitro nucleic acid biochemistry.

title: Syntactic Structures
authors: Chomsky N
summary: Introduced transformational generative grammar and formal language hierarchies, reshaping linguistics and early symbolic NLP.

title: Dynamic Programming
authors: Bellman R
summary: Introduced dynamic programming, the principle of optimality and the Bellman equation for sequential decision problems. Value functions and Bellman backups underlie nearly every RL algorithm.

title: Intravenous infusion of bone marrow in patients receiving radiation and chemotherapy
authors: Thomas ED, Lochte HL Jr, Lu WC, Ferrebee JW
summary: Early human bone marrow infusion studies that founded hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the first cell therapy (Nobel 1990).

title: A three-dimensional model of the myoglobin molecule obtained by X-ray analysis
authors: Kendrew JC, Bodo G, Dintzis HM, Parrish RG, Wyckoff H, Phillips DC
summary: The first three-dimensional structure of a protein (myoglobin), proving that protein structures could be solved by X-ray crystallography.

title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
authors: Rosenblatt F
summary: Introduced the perceptron, a trainable threshold unit with an error-correcting learning rule and convergence guarantees for linearly separable data.

title: On protein synthesis
authors: Crick FHC
venue: Symposia of the Society for Experimental Biology 12:138-163
summary: Set out the sequence hypothesis, the adaptor hypothesis and the central dogma of information flow from DNA to RNA to protein.

title: The replication of DNA in Escherichia coli
authors: Meselson M, Stahl FW
summary: Density-gradient labelling showed DNA replicates semiconservatively, confirming the strand-separation prediction of the double helix.

title: Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers
authors: Samuel AL
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development 3(3):210-229
summary: A checkers program that improved through self-play by adjusting its evaluation function toward later positions' values, an early form of temporal-difference learning. It popularized the term 'machine learning'.

title: Structure of haemoglobin: a three-dimensional Fourier synthesis at 5.5-Å resolution, obtained by X-ray analysis
authors: Perutz MF, Rossmann MG, Cullis AF, Muirhead H, Will G, North ACT
summary: Solved haemoglobin using heavy-atom isomorphous replacement, opening the way to structure-function understanding of allostery; Nobel Prize 1962 with Kendrew.

title: Adaptive Switching Circuits
authors: Widrow B, Hoff ME
summary: Introduced ADALINE and the least-mean-squares (delta) rule, gradient descent on a squared error that prefigures modern training.

title: Dynamic Programming and Markov Processes
authors: Howard RA
summary: Formalized Markov decision processes and introduced policy iteration, alternating policy evaluation and greedy improvement. Policy iteration is the template for generalized policy iteration in RL.

title: Immunoassay of endogenous plasma insulin in man
authors: Yalow RS, Berson SA
summary: Introduced radioimmunoassay for measuring hormones at picomolar concentrations (Nobel 1977).

title: An unstable intermediate carrying information from genes to ribosomes for protein synthesis
authors: Brenner S, Jacob F, Meselson M
summary: Demonstrated a short-lived RNA messenger that carries genetic information to pre-existing ribosomes, establishing mRNA.

title: General nature of the genetic code for proteins
authors: Crick FHC, Barnett L, Brenner S, Watts-Tobin RJ
summary: Frameshift mutant analysis in phage T4 showed the code is read in non-overlapping triplets from a fixed starting point.

title: Genetic regulatory mechanisms in the synthesis of proteins
authors: Jacob F, Monod J
summary: The operon model of coordinated gene regulation by repressors acting on operators, founding the study of gene expression control.

title: The dependence of cell-free protein synthesis in E. coli upon naturally occurring or synthetic polyribonucleotides
authors: Nirenberg MW, Matthaei JH
summary: Poly(U) directed synthesis of polyphenylalanine in a cell-free extract, cracking the first codon and opening the way to the genetic code.

title: Oral poliovirus vaccine (Sabin strains) licensed in the United States
authors: Sabin AB
summary: Live attenuated oral polio vaccine providing mucosal immunity and easy mass administration, the workhorse of global polio eradication.

title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
authors: Hubel DH, Wiesel TN
summary: Characterized simple and complex cells and hierarchical receptive fields in visual cortex, inspiring hierarchical feature models from the Neocognitron to CNNs.

title: Stereochemistry of polypeptide chain configurations
authors: Ramachandran GN, Ramakrishnan C, Sasisekharan V
summary: Introduced the Ramachandran plot of allowed backbone phi/psi angles, still the basic validation of protein structures and a constraint for prediction.

title: Machine Perception of Three-Dimensional Solids
authors: Roberts LG
summary: The 'blocks world' thesis: extracted edges from photographs and matched them to 3D polyhedral models, often cited as the start of computer vision.

title: Experiments on the Mechanization of Game-Learning Part I. Characterization of the Model and its Parameters
authors: Michie D
summary: MENACE, a 'machine' of matchboxes filled with colored beads, learned to play noughts and crosses by reinforcing the moves that led to wins. A vivid early demonstration of trial-and-error learning.

title: p-σ-π Analysis. A method for the correlation of biological activity and chemical structure
authors: Hansch C, Fujita T
summary: Founded QSAR by regressing biological activity on hydrophobic, electronic and steric descriptors, the start of computational drug design.

title: RNA codewords and protein synthesis: the effect of trinucleotides upon the binding of sRNA to ribosomes
authors: Nirenberg M, Leder P
summary: The triplet-binding assay that allowed systematic assignment of codons and, with Khorana's synthetic polymers, completion of the genetic code.

title: Atlas of Protein Sequence and Structure
authors: Dayhoff MO, Eck RV, Chang MA, Sochard MR
summary: The first comprehensive compilation of protein sequences, effectively the first bioinformatics database and the template for later sequence databanks.

title: Structure of a ribonucleic acid
authors: Holley RW, Apgar J, Everett GA, Madison JT, Marquisee M, Merrill SH, et al.
summary: First complete sequence of a nucleic acid, yeast alanine tRNA, identifying the adaptor molecule Crick had postulated.

title: A "new" antigen in leukemia sera
authors: Blumberg BS, Alter HJ, Visnich S
summary: Discovered the Australia antigen (HBsAg), enabling hepatitis B blood screening and later the hepatitis B vaccine.

title: ELIZA—A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication between Man and Machine
authors: Weizenbaum J
summary: Pattern-matching chatbot that simulated a Rogerian therapist, the first widely known conversational program and an early lesson in anthropomorphism.

title: Enzymatic breakage and joining of deoxyribonucleic acid, I. Repair of single-strand breaks in DNA by an enzyme from E. coli infected with T4 bacteriophage
authors: Weiss B, Richardson CC
summary: Characterised DNA ligase, the enzyme that seals DNA backbones and became the essential joining reagent of recombinant DNA work.

title: DNA restriction enzyme from E. coli
authors: Meselson M, Yuan R
summary: Isolated the first restriction enzyme activity, giving biochemical substance to Arber's host-controlled restriction and modification.

title: BOXES: An Experiment in Adaptive Control
authors: Michie D, Chambers RA
summary: Learned to balance a pole on a cart by partitioning the state space into 'boxes', each with its own learned action, using only failure signals. An early demonstration of RL for control and the benchmark later used by actor-critic work.

title: How to fold graciously
authors: Levinthal C
venue: Mössbauer Spectroscopy in Biological Systems, Univ. Illinois Press, pp. 22-24
summary: Posed Levinthal's paradox: random conformational search would take astronomically long, so folding must follow guided pathways.

title: Metabolic stability and epigenesis in randomly constructed genetic nets
authors: Kauffman SA
summary: Introduced random Boolean networks as models of gene regulation, linking attractors to cell types.

title: Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry
authors: Minsky M, Papert S
summary: Rigorously analyzed the limits of single-layer perceptrons (e.g., parity, XOR, connectedness), contributing to a long decline in neural-network funding.

title: A general method applicable to the search for similarities in the amino acid sequence of two proteins
authors: Needleman SB, Wunsch CD
summary: Introduced dynamic programming for optimal global alignment of two sequences, the algorithmic foundation of sequence comparison.

title: The Representation of the Cumulative Rounding Error of an Algorithm as a Taylor Expansion of the Local Rounding Errors
authors: Linnainmaa S
summary: First description of reverse-mode automatic differentiation, the general algorithm underlying backpropagation.

title: A restriction enzyme from Hemophilus influenzae. I. Purification and general properties
authors: Smith HO, Wilcox KW
summary: Purified HindII, the first sequence-specific restriction endonuclease, providing the molecular scissors that made DNA cloning possible.

title: RNA-dependent DNA polymerase in virions of RNA tumour viruses
authors: Baltimore D
summary: Independent demonstration of reverse transcriptase, the enzyme that later made cDNA cloning and much of molecular biology possible.

title: RNA-dependent DNA polymerase in virions of Rous sarcoma virus
authors: Temin HM, Mizutani S
summary: Discovery of reverse transcriptase in an RNA tumour virus, showing information can flow from RNA back to DNA.

title: Specific cleavage of simian virus 40 DNA by restriction endonuclease of Hemophilus influenzae
authors: Danna K, Nathans D
summary: Used a restriction enzyme to cut a viral genome into defined fragments, producing the first physical restriction map of a DNA molecule.

title: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Quantitative assay of immunoglobulin G
authors: Engvall E, Perlmann P
summary: Invented ELISA, replacing radioisotopes with enzyme labels and becoming the most widely used immunodiagnostic format.

title: Biochemical method for inserting new genetic information into DNA of simian virus 40: circular SV40 DNA molecules containing lambda phage genes and the galactose operon of Escherichia coli
authors: Jackson DA, Symons RH, Berg P
summary: First construction of a recombinant DNA molecule in vitro, joining viral and bacterial DNA and creating the field of genetic engineering.

title: Understanding Natural Language
authors: Winograd T
summary: Described SHRDLU, a system that understood and executed English commands in a blocks world by integrating syntax, semantics and reasoning.

title: Principles that govern the folding of protein chains
authors: Anfinsen CB
summary: Nobel lecture stating the thermodynamic hypothesis: the amino acid sequence determines the native structure, the premise of structure prediction.

title: Construction of biologically functional bacterial plasmids in vitro
authors: Cohen SN, Chang AC, Boyer HW, Helling RB
summary: Built recombinant plasmids that replicated and expressed their inserted genes in E. coli, making molecular cloning a practical, general technology.

title: Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences
authors: Werbos PJ
summary: Proposed applying reverse-mode gradient computation to train multilayer neural networks, an early formulation of backpropagation.

title: A rapid method for determining sequences in DNA by primed synthesis with DNA polymerase
authors: Sanger F, Coulson AR
summary: The 'plus and minus' method, Sanger's first practical enzymatic DNA sequencing approach using primed polymerase synthesis.

title: Detection of specific sequences among DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis
authors: Southern EM
summary: The Southern blot: transfer of electrophoresed DNA to a membrane and detection by hybridisation, the workhorse assay of early gene analysis.

title: Summary statement of the Asilomar Conference on recombinant DNA molecules
authors: Berg P, Baltimore D, Brenner S, Roblin RO, Singer MF
summary: The Asilomar consensus on containment-based self-governance of recombinant DNA research, the template for later biotechnology governance.

title: Continuous cultures of fused cells secreting antibody of predefined specificity
authors: Köhler G, Milstein C
summary: Invented hybridoma technology for producing monoclonal antibodies of a single defined specificity, the foundation of antibody therapeutics and immunodiagnostics.

title: Dynamics of folded proteins
authors: McCammon JA, Gelin BR, Karplus M
summary: The first molecular dynamics simulation of a protein (BPTI), revealing internal fluid-like motions.

title: The Protein Data Bank: a computer-based archival file for macromolecular structures
authors: Bernstein FC, Koetzle TF, Williams GJ, Meyer EF Jr, Brice MD, Rodgers JR, et al.
summary: Described the Protein Data Bank archive founded in 1971, the shared repository of macromolecular coordinates.

title: A new method for sequencing DNA
authors: Maxam AM, Gilbert W
summary: Chemical-cleavage DNA sequencing using base-specific reactions on end-labelled DNA; one of the two founding sequencing methods.

title: DNA sequencing with chain-terminating inhibitors
authors: Sanger F, Nicklen S, Coulson AR
summary: Introduced dideoxy chain-termination sequencing, the dominant DNA sequencing method for three decades and the basis of the Human Genome Project.

title: Nucleotide sequence of bacteriophage phiX174 DNA
authors: Sanger F, Air GM, Barrell BG, Brown NL, Coulson AR, Fiddes JC, et al.
summary: First complete DNA genome (5,386 nt), revealing overlapping genes.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of a chemically synthesized gene for the hormone somatostatin
authors: Itakura K, Hirose T, Crea R, Riggs AD, Heyneker HL, Bolivar F, et al.
summary: First bacterial expression of a chemically synthesised gene encoding a human peptide hormone, the proof of concept for recombinant pharmaceuticals.

title: Spliced segments at the 5' terminus of adenovirus 2 late mRNA
authors: Berget SM, Moore C, Sharp PA
summary: Showed mRNA is assembled from discontinuous genomic segments, revealing RNA splicing and introns in eukaryotic gene expression.

title: Stable incorporation of plasmid DNA into higher plant cells: the molecular basis of crown gall tumorigenesis
authors: Chilton MD, Drummond MH, Merlo DJ, Sciaky D, Montoya AL, Gordon MP, et al.
summary: Showed Agrobacterium transfers Ti-plasmid DNA into the plant genome, revealing nature's own plant transformation vector.

title: A model of evolutionary change in proteins
authors: Dayhoff MO, Schwartz RM, Orcutt BC
venue: Atlas of Protein Sequence and Structure 5(Suppl 3):345-352
summary: Introduced the PAM (point accepted mutation) substitution matrices derived from closely related sequences, the standard scoring scheme for protein alignment for decades.

title: Mutagenesis at a specific position in a DNA sequence
authors: Hutchison CA 3rd, Phillips S, Edgell MH, Gillam S, Jahnke P, Smith M
summary: Used a synthetic mismatched oligonucleotide to introduce a predetermined point mutation, inventing oligonucleotide-directed site-specific mutagenesis.

title: Inhibition of Rous sarcoma virus replication and cell transformation by a specific oligodeoxynucleotide
authors: Zamecnik PC, Stephenson ML
summary: First demonstration that a synthetic antisense oligonucleotide can inhibit gene expression, founding antisense therapeutics.

title: Direct expression in Escherichia coli of a DNA sequence coding for human growth hormone
authors: Goeddel DV, Heyneker HL, Hozumi T, Arentzen R, Itakura K, Yansura DG, et al.
summary: Recombinant human growth hormone produced in bacteria, which replaced cadaver-derived hGH after prion contamination was discovered.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of chemically synthesized genes for human insulin
authors: Goeddel DV, Kleid DG, Bolivar F, Heyneker HL, Yansura DG, Crea R, et al.
summary: Genentech's recombinant production of human insulin A and B chains in E. coli, leading to Humulin (1982), the first approved recombinant drug and the start of the biotech industry.

title: Neocognitron: A Self-Organizing Neural Network Model for a Mechanism of Pattern Recognition Unaffected by Shift in Position
authors: Fukushima K
summary: Hierarchical network of alternating feature-extracting and pooling layers inspired by visual cortex; the architectural precursor of convolutional networks.

title: Genetic transformation of mouse embryos by microinjection of purified DNA
authors: Gordon JW, Scangos GA, Plotkin DJ, Barbosa JA, Ruddle FH
summary: First transgenic mice made by pronuclear microinjection, extending recombinant DNA from microbes to whole animals.

title: Process for producing biologically functional molecular chimeras (US Patent 4,237,224)
authors: Cohen SN, Boyer HW
venue: United States Patent and Trademark Office
summary: The Cohen-Boyer gene-splicing patent, licensed broadly to industry and the commercial foundation of the biotechnology sector.

title: Preparation, characterization, and immunogenicity of Haemophilus influenzae type b polysaccharide-protein conjugates
authors: Schneerson R, Barrera O, Sutton A, Robbins JB
summary: Conjugating capsular polysaccharide to a carrier protein made it immunogenic in infants, the basis of Hib, pneumococcal and meningococcal conjugate vaccines.

title: Evolutionary trees from DNA sequences: a maximum likelihood approach
authors: Felsenstein J
summary: Introduced practical maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference with the pruning algorithm, the statistical foundation of modern molecular phylogenetics.

title: Identification of common molecular subsequences
authors: Smith TF, Waterman MS
summary: Adapted dynamic programming to find optimal local alignments, the rigorous basis for detecting shared domains and for database search.

title: A computer algorithm for reconstructing a scene from two projections
authors: Longuet-Higgins HC
summary: Introduced the essential matrix and the eight-point algorithm for two-view relative pose and structure recovery.

title: An Iterative Image Registration Technique with an Application to Stereo Vision
authors: Lucas BD, Kanade T
summary: Local least-squares, gradient-based image alignment (Lucas-Kanade), the basis of sparse optical flow and feature tracking.

title: Determining Optical Flow
authors: Horn BKP, Schunck BG
summary: Global variational optical flow method combining brightness constancy with a smoothness prior; the foundation of dense flow estimation.

title: Random Sample Consensus: A Paradigm for Model Fitting with Applications to Image Analysis and Automated Cartography
authors: Fischler MA, Bolles RC
summary: RANSAC: robust model fitting by hypothesize-and-verify on random minimal samples; ubiquitous in geometric vision.

title: Establishment in culture of pluripotential cells from mouse embryos
authors: Evans MJ, Kaufman MH
summary: Derived mouse embryonic stem cells, enabling gene targeting and the field of pluripotent stem cell biology.

title: Isolation of a pluripotent cell line from early mouse embryos cultured in medium conditioned by teratocarcinoma stem cells
authors: Martin GR
summary: Independent derivation of mouse ES cells; coined the term 'embryonic stem cell'.

title: A geometric approach to macromolecule-ligand interactions
authors: Kuntz ID, Blaney JM, Oatley SJ, Langridge R, Ferrin TE
summary: Introduced DOCK, the first molecular docking program, matching ligand shapes to receptor sites for structure-based drug design.

title: Vision: A Computational Investigation into the Human Representation and Processing of Visual Information
authors: Marr D
summary: Framed vision as information processing across computational, algorithmic and implementation levels, with the primal sketch / 2.5D sketch / 3D model pipeline that shaped decades of research.

title: Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities
authors: Hopfield JJ
summary: Introduced Hopfield networks: recurrent networks with an energy function that act as content-addressable memories, linking neural computation to statistical physics.

title: Nucleotide sequence of bacteriophage lambda DNA
authors: Sanger F, Coulson AR, Hong GF, Hill DF, Petersen GB
summary: 48.5 kb lambda genome sequenced by random shotgun cloning, establishing shotgun sequencing.

title: Dramatic growth of mice that develop from eggs microinjected with metallothionein-growth hormone fusion genes
authors: Palmiter RD, Brinster RL, Hammer RE, Trumbauer ME, Rosenfeld MG, Birnberg NC, et al.
summary: A regulated transgene produced a dramatic whole-animal phenotype, establishing transgenic animals as tools for studying gene function and expression.

title: Synthesis and assembly of hepatitis B virus surface antigen particles in yeast
authors: Valenzuela P, Medina A, Rutter WJ, Ammerer G, Hall BD
summary: Yeast-expressed HBsAg self-assembled into particles, leading to the first recombinant vaccine (hepatitis B, licensed 1986).

title: Expression of chimaeric genes transferred into plant nuclei using a Ti-plasmid-derived vector
authors: Herrera-Estrella L, Depicker A, Van Montagu M, Schell J
summary: Disarmed Ti plasmids delivered and expressed a selectable chimaeric gene in plant nuclei, creating the first transgenic plants.

title: Neuronlike Adaptive Elements That Can Solve Difficult Learning Control Problems
authors: Barto AG, Sutton RS, Anderson CW
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics SMC-13(5):834-846
summary: Introduced the actor-critic architecture: an adaptive critic learns a value estimate (an early form of TD) that trains an actor through a reinforcement signal. It solved the cart-pole balancing task and set the template for actor-critic methods.

title: Hybrid hybridomas and their use in immunohistochemistry
authors: Milstein C, Cuello AC
summary: Fused two hybridomas ('quadromas') to produce bispecific antibodies, the conceptual origin of bispecific antibody therapeutics.

title: Chimeric human antibody molecules: mouse antigen-binding domains with human constant region domains
authors: Morrison SL, Johnson MJ, Herzenberg LA, Oi VT
summary: Engineered mouse-human chimeric antibodies to reduce immunogenicity, the format later used by rituximab and infliximab.

title: Solution conformation of proteinase inhibitor IIA from bull seminal plasma by 1H nuclear magnetic resonance and distance geometry
authors: Williamson MP, Havel TF, Wüthrich K
summary: The first complete protein structure determined by NMR in solution, establishing NMR as a second route to atomic protein structures (Wüthrich, Nobel 2002).

title: A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines
authors: Ackley DH, Hinton GE, Sejnowski TJ
summary: Introduced Boltzmann machines, stochastic networks with hidden units trained by a local learning rule, an early probabilistic generative neural model.

title: A simple and general method for transferring genes into plants
authors: Horsch RB, Fry JE, Hoffmann NL, Eichholtz D, Rogers SG, Fraley RT
summary: The leaf-disc transformation protocol that made routine production of transgenic plants practical for laboratories everywhere.

title: Enzymatic amplification of beta-globin genomic sequences and restriction site analysis for diagnosis of sickle cell anemia
authors: Saiki RK, Scharf S, Faloona F, Mullis KB, Horn GT, Erlich HA, et al.
summary: First published application of the polymerase chain reaction, amplifying a human gene segment for genetic diagnosis.

title: Filamentous fusion phage: novel expression vectors that display cloned antigens on the virion surface
authors: Smith GP
summary: Invented phage display, physically linking a peptide to the gene encoding it so vast libraries can be selected by binding.

title: Insertion of DNA sequences into the human chromosomal beta-globin locus by homologous recombination
authors: Smithies O, Gregg RG, Boggs SS, Koralewski MA, Kucherlapati RS
summary: Showed exogenous DNA can be targeted to a chosen chromosomal locus in mammalian cells by homologous recombination, the origin of gene targeting.

title: Cloning and expression of the human erythropoietin gene
authors: Lin FK, Suggs S, Lin CH, Browne JK, Smalling R, Egrie JC, et al.
summary: Amgen's cloning and mammalian-cell expression of human EPO, yielding epoetin alfa, one of the most commercially successful early biologics.

title: The GenBank genetic sequence databank
authors: Bilofsky HS, Burks C, Fickett JW, Goad WB, Lewitter FI, Rindone WP, et al.
summary: Described GenBank, the public nucleotide sequence archive established in 1982 at Los Alamos and later run by NCBI, a core shared resource of genomics.

title: A Computational Approach to Edge Detection
authors: Canny J
summary: Derived an optimal edge detector with non-maximum suppression and hysteresis thresholding; still the standard edge detector.

title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
authors: Rumelhart DE, Hinton GE, Williams RJ
summary: Demonstrated that backpropagation trains multilayer networks to learn useful internal representations, overcoming perceptron limitations and reviving the field.

title: Fluorescence detection in automated DNA sequence analysis
authors: Smith LM, Sanders JZ, Kaiser RJ, Hughes P, Dodd C, Connell CR, et al.
summary: Four-colour fluorescent primers with laser detection enabled automated Sanger sequencing, leading to the first commercial sequencers.

title: Engineering herbicide tolerance in transgenic plants
authors: Shah DM, Horsch RB, Klee HJ, Kishore GM, Winter JA, Tumer NE, et al.
summary: Overexpression of an EPSP synthase gene gave glyphosate tolerance, the research line that became Roundup Ready crops.

title: Replacing the complementarity-determining regions in a human antibody with those from a mouse
authors: Jones PT, Dear PH, Foote J, Neuberger MS, Winter G
summary: Introduced CDR grafting to humanize antibodies, enabling a generation of therapeutics such as trastuzumab and many others.

title: Spin glasses and the statistical mechanics of protein folding
authors: Bryngelson JD, Wolynes PG
summary: Introduced energy-landscape theory and the principle of minimal frustration, resolving Levinthal's paradox via funneled landscapes.

title: High-velocity microprojectiles for delivering nucleic acids into living cells
authors: Klein TM, Wolf ED, Wu R, Sanford JC
summary: The gene gun delivered DNA into cells physically, opening transformation of cereals and organelles that Agrobacterium could not reach.

title: Nucleotide sequence of the iap gene, responsible for alkaline phosphatase isozyme conversion in Escherichia coli, and identification of the gene product
authors: Ishino Y, Shinagawa H, Makino K, Amemura M, Nakata A
summary: Incidentally reported the first CRISPR array: an unexplained set of interspaced repeats downstream of the E. coli iap gene.

title: Site-directed mutagenesis by gene targeting in mouse embryo-derived stem cells
authors: Thomas KR, Capecchi MR
summary: Gene targeting in embryonic stem cells, the route to knockout mice and to systematic reverse genetics in mammals.

title: Transgenic plants protected from insect attack
authors: Vaeck M, Reynaerts A, Höfte H, Jansens S, De Beuckeleer M, Dean C, et al.
summary: Expressed a Bacillus thuringiensis toxin gene in tobacco to kill feeding larvae, the origin of Bt insect-resistant crops.

title: Cryo-electron microscopy of vitrified specimens
authors: Dubochet J, Adrian M, Chang JJ, Homo JC, Lepault J, McDowall AW, et al.
summary: Established vitrification of thin aqueous specimens in amorphous ice, the sample preparation underlying all biological cryo-EM (Nobel 2017).

title: Improved tools for biological sequence comparison
authors: Pearson WR, Lipman DJ
summary: Introduced the FASTA program, a fast k-tuple heuristic for sensitive database similarity search that preceded BLAST.

title: A Combined Corner and Edge Detector
authors: Harris C, Stephens M
summary: The Harris corner detector based on the local structure tensor, a foundational interest-point detector for matching and tracking.

title: Snakes: Active Contour Models
authors: Kass M, Witkin A, Terzopoulos D
summary: Energy-minimizing deformable contours for boundary extraction, launching the variational / active contour approach to segmentation.

title: Laser desorption ionization of proteins with molecular masses exceeding 10,000 daltons
authors: Karas M, Hillenkamp F
summary: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionisation (MALDI) of large proteins.

title: Protein and polymer analyses up to m/z 100 000 by laser ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry
authors: Tanaka K, Waki H, Ido Y, Akita S, Yoshida Y, Yoshida T
summary: Soft laser desorption ionisation of intact proteins (Nobel Prize 2002), alongside MALDI by Karas and Hillenkamp.

title: Primer-directed enzymatic amplification of DNA with a thermostable DNA polymerase
authors: Saiki RK, Gelfand DH, Stoffel S, Scharf SJ, Higuchi R, Horn GT, et al.
summary: Introduced Taq polymerase into PCR, giving specificity, long products and automation and turning PCR into universal laboratory infrastructure.

title: Reduction of polygalacturonase activity in tomato fruit by antisense RNA
authors: Sheehy RE, Kramer M, Hiatt WR
summary: Antisense suppression of a ripening enzyme slowed tomato softening, the science behind the Flavr Savr tomato.

title: A Stochastic Parts Program and Noun Phrase Parser for Unrestricted Text
authors: Church KW
venue: Proc. 2nd Conference on Applied Natural Language Processing (ANLP 1988)
summary: Showed that a simple HMM-style statistical tagger trained on corpora achieves high part-of-speech accuracy, helping launch the empirical turn in NLP.

title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences
authors: Sutton RS
summary: Formalized temporal-difference (TD) learning, which updates predictions from the difference between successive estimates instead of waiting for final outcomes. It introduced TD(lambda), proved convergence results, and became a core mechanism of RL.

title: Clearblue One Step: first lateral-flow home pregnancy test
authors: Unilever
summary: Monoclonal-antibody lateral-flow immunoassay for hCG, popularizing the rapid test format later used for COVID-19 antigen tests.

title: Use of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and interleukin-2 in the immunotherapy of patients with metastatic melanoma
authors: Rosenberg SA, Packard BS, Aebersold PM, Solomon D, Topalian SL, Toy ST, et al.
summary: Adoptive transfer of expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes caused melanoma regressions, founding adoptive T-cell therapy.

title: Backpropagation Applied to Handwritten Zip Code Recognition
authors: LeCun Y, Boser B, Denker JS, Henderson D, Howard RE, Hubbard W, et al.
summary: Trained a convolutional network end-to-end with backpropagation on real zip-code digits, establishing the modern CNN.

title: Approximation by Superpositions of a Sigmoidal Function
authors: Cybenko G
venue: Mathematics of Control, Signals and Systems 2:303-314
summary: Proved single-hidden-layer networks with sigmoidal units can approximate any continuous function on a compact set (universal approximation).

title: Multilayer Feedforward Networks are Universal Approximators
authors: Hornik K, Stinchcombe M, White H
summary: Established universal approximation for multilayer feedforward networks with general squashing activations.

title: Electrospray ionization for mass spectrometry of large biomolecules
authors: Fenn JB, Mann M, Meng CK, Wong SF, Whitehouse CM
summary: Electrospray ionisation producing multiply charged ions of large biomolecules (Nobel Prize 2002), enabling LC-MS/MS proteomics.

title: A general method for site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids into proteins
authors: Noren CJ, Anthony-Cahill SJ, Griffith MC, Schultz PG
summary: Chemically acylated suppressor tRNA allowed non-natural amino acids to be read into proteins in vitro, the start of genetic code expansion.

title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition
authors: Rabiner LR
summary: Canonical exposition of HMM inference and training (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch), the workhorse of speech and tagging for decades.

title: ALVINN: An Autonomous Land Vehicle in a Neural Network
authors: Pomerleau DA
venue: NIPS 1988 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 1)
summary: A neural network learned to steer a vehicle from camera images by imitating a human driver. It is the classic example of behavior cloning and of the distribution shift problem it suffers from.

title: Cationic liposome-mediated RNA transfection
authors: Malone RW, Felgner PL, Verma IM
summary: Delivered mRNA into cells with cationic lipids and observed protein expression, an early step toward lipid-delivered mRNA medicines.

title: Basic local alignment search tool
authors: Altschul SF, Gish W, Miller W, Myers EW, Lipman DJ
summary: Introduced BLAST, a fast seed-and-extend heuristic with rigorous statistics for local alignment search, becoming one of the most-used tools in biology.

title: Model for the structure of bacteriorhodopsin based on high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy
authors: Henderson R, Baldwin JM, Ceska TA, Zemlin F, Beckmann E, Downing KH
summary: The first atomic model of a membrane protein from electron cryo-microscopy, showing EM could reach near-atomic resolution (Nobel 2017).

title: Finding Structure in Time
authors: Elman JL
summary: Introduced the simple recurrent (Elman) network with context units and showed it learns temporal and grammatical structure.

title: Phage antibodies: filamentous phage displaying antibody variable domains
authors: McCafferty J, Griffiths AD, Winter G, Chiswell DJ
summary: Displayed antibody fragments on phage, enabling fully in vitro selection of human antibodies and a generation of antibody drugs.

title: Indexing by Latent Semantic Analysis
authors: Deerwester S, Dumais ST, Furnas GW, Landauer TK, Harshman R
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science 41(6):391-407
summary: Used truncated SVD of term-document matrices to obtain latent semantic vectors, an early dense distributional representation for retrieval.

title: Integrated Architectures for Learning, Planning, and Reacting Based on Approximating Dynamic Programming
authors: Sutton RS
venue: Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 1990)
summary: Introduced Dyna, which learns a world model from experience and uses simulated transitions from it for extra value updates. It is the archetype of model-based RL that interleaves learning and planning.

title: Direct gene transfer into mouse muscle in vivo
authors: Wolff JA, Malone RW, Williams P, Chong W, Acsadi G, Jani A, et al.
summary: Showed naked mRNA and plasmid DNA injected into muscle are expressed in vivo, the conceptual origin of mRNA and DNA vaccines.

title: Eigenfaces for Recognition
authors: Turk M, Pentland A
summary: Face recognition by projecting images onto principal components ('eigenfaces'), a landmark of appearance-based recognition.

title: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts
authors: Jacobs RA, Jordan MI, Nowlan SJ, Hinton GE
summary: Introduced mixture of experts: a gating network routes inputs to specialized expert networks, the ancestor of sparse MoE layers.

title: Complementary DNA sequencing: expressed sequence tags and human genome project
authors: Adams MD, Kelley JM, Gocayne JD, Dubnick M, Polymeropoulos MH, Xiao H, et al.
summary: Expressed sequence tags (ESTs): rapid partial cDNA sequencing for gene discovery.

title: Light-directed, spatially addressable parallel chemical synthesis
authors: Fodor SP, Read JL, Pirrung MC, Stryer L, Lu AT, Solas D
summary: Photolithographic in situ synthesis of high-density peptide and oligonucleotide arrays, the basis of Affymetrix GeneChips.

title: Detection of specific polymerase chain reaction product by utilizing the 5'→3' exonuclease activity of Thermus aquaticus DNA polymerase
authors: Holland PM, Abramson RD, Watson R, Gelfand DH
summary: Introduced the 5' nuclease (TaqMan) probe principle for sequence-specific PCR detection.

title: A new approach to protein fold recognition
authors: Jones DT, Taylor WR, Thornton JM
summary: Introduced threading, scoring sequence fit to known folds with pairwise potentials, to recognize folds beyond detectable homology.

title: Amino acid substitution matrices from protein blocks
authors: Henikoff S, Henikoff JG
summary: Derived the BLOSUM substitution matrices from conserved blocks of distant homologs; BLOSUM62 became the default protein scoring matrix.

title: DNA sequencing using capillary array electrophoresis
authors: Huang XC, Quesada MA, Mathies RA
summary: Capillary array electrophoresis for parallel fluorescent sequencing; basis of the capillary instruments (e.g. ABI 3700) that sequenced the human genome.

title: Q-learning
authors: Watkins CJCH, Dayan P
summary: Proved convergence of Q-learning, the off-policy TD control algorithm from Watkins' 1989 thesis that learns optimal action values regardless of the behavior policy. Q-learning is the basis of DQN and most value-based RL.

title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning
authors: Williams RJ
summary: Introduced REINFORCE, which estimates the gradient of expected reward with the likelihood-ratio trick and a baseline. It is the root of all policy gradient methods, including those used to fine-tune LLMs.

title: Induced expression of PD-1, a novel member of the immunoglobulin gene superfamily, upon programmed cell death
authors: Ishida Y, Agata Y, Shibahara K, Honjo T
summary: Discovered PD-1, later shown to be an inhibitory immune checkpoint and the target of anti-PD-1 therapies (Nobel 2018).

title: Isolation and characterization of exendin-4, an exendin-3 analogue, from Heloderma suspectum venom
authors: Eng J, Kleinman WA, Singh L, Singh G, Raufman JP
summary: Discovered exendin-4 in Gila monster venom, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that became exenatide, the first GLP-1 drug.

title: Papillomavirus L1 major capsid protein self-assembles into virus-like particles that are highly immunogenic
authors: Kirnbauer R, Booy F, Cheng N, Lowy DR, Schiller JT
summary: Showed recombinant L1 forms highly immunogenic virus-like particles, the basis of HPV vaccines.

title: Comparative protein modelling by satisfaction of spatial restraints
authors: Šali A, Blundell TL
summary: Introduced MODELLER, the standard homology-modeling approach that builds models from template-derived spatial restraints.

title: Prediction of protein secondary structure at better than 70% accuracy
authors: Rost B, Sander C
summary: PHD combined neural networks with multiple sequence alignment profiles, a decisive early use of evolutionary information and machine learning for prediction.

title: Tuning the activity of an enzyme for unusual environments: sequential random mutagenesis of subtilisin E for catalysis in dimethylformamide
authors: Chen K, Arnold FH
summary: Iterated rounds of random mutagenesis and screening improved an enzyme far beyond rational design, establishing directed evolution of proteins.

title: Building a Large Annotated Corpus of English: The Penn Treebank
authors: Marcus MP, Santorini B, Marcinkiewicz MA
summary: Released a large POS-tagged and syntactically bracketed corpus that became the standard training and benchmark resource for tagging and parsing.

title: The Mathematics of Statistical Machine Translation: Parameter Estimation
authors: Brown PF, Della Pietra SA, Della Pietra VJ, Mercer RL
summary: Defined IBM Models 1-5 for word alignment and translation trained with EM, the foundation of SMT for two decades.

title: Kinetic PCR analysis: real-time monitoring of DNA amplification reactions
authors: Higuchi R, Fockler C, Dollinger G, Watson R
summary: Real-time quantitative PCR via fluorescence monitoring, now the gold standard for molecular diagnostics.

title: Specific activation and targeting of cytotoxic lymphocytes through chimeric single chains consisting of antibody-binding domains and the gamma or zeta subunits of the immunoglobulin and T-cell receptors
authors: Eshhar Z, Waks T, Gross G, Schindler DG
summary: Created the single-chain chimeric antigen receptor (scFv fused to CD3ζ), the blueprint of CAR-T cells.

title: CLUSTAL W: improving the sensitivity of progressive multiple sequence alignment through sequence weighting, position-specific gap penalties and weight matrix choice
authors: Thompson JD, Higgins DG, Gibson TJ
summary: The widely used progressive multiple sequence alignment program, making MSAs routine for evolutionary and structural analysis.

title: Hidden Markov models in computational biology: applications to protein modeling
authors: Krogh A, Brown M, Mian IS, Sjölander K, Haussler D
summary: Introduced profile hidden Markov models for protein families, giving a probabilistic framework for homology detection and alignment.

title: Stoichiometric flux balance models quantitatively predict growth and metabolic by-product secretion in wild-type Escherichia coli W3110
authors: Varma A, Palsson BO
summary: Showed constraint-based flux balance analysis predicts E. coli growth and secretion quantitatively, launching genome-scale metabolic modeling.

title: Learning Long-Term Dependencies with Gradient Descent is Difficult
authors: Bengio Y, Simard P, Frasconi P
summary: Analyzed vanishing and exploding gradients in recurrent networks, explaining why long-range dependencies are hard to learn.

title: An approach to correlate tandem mass spectral data of peptides with amino acid sequences in a protein database
authors: Eng JK, McCormack AL, Yates JR
summary: SEQUEST database search matching MS/MS spectra to sequences, the basis of shotgun proteomics.

title: FDA clearance of the Flavr Savr tomato, the first genetically engineered whole food
authors: US Food and Drug Administration
venue: US Food and Drug Administration decision; Calgene Inc.
summary: First regulatory clearance of a transgenic food crop for sale, setting the precedent for GM food review in the United States.

title: Green fluorescent protein as a marker for gene expression
authors: Chalfie M, Tu Y, Euskirchen G, Ward WW, Prasher DC
summary: Showed GFP fluoresces when expressed heterologously, creating a genetically encoded reporter that transformed cell and developmental biology.

title: Introduction of double-strand breaks into the genome of mouse cells by expression of a rare-cutting endonuclease
authors: Rouet P, Smih F, Jasin M
summary: Showed a targeted double-strand break made by a meganuclease greatly stimulates recombination at that site, the founding principle of nuclease-based genome editing.

title: Rapid evolution of a protein in vitro by DNA shuffling
authors: Stemmer WPC
summary: Added in vitro recombination to directed evolution, letting beneficial mutations from different variants be combined efficiently.

title: Markov Games as a Framework for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Littman ML
summary: Framed multi-agent RL as learning in Markov (stochastic) games and introduced minimax-Q for two-player zero-sum settings. A foundation of multi-agent RL.

title: On-Line Q-Learning Using Connectionist Systems
authors: Rummery GA, Niranjan M
venue: Technical Report CUED/F-INFENG/TR 166, Cambridge University Engineering Department
summary: Introduced the on-policy TD control algorithm later named SARSA, which updates toward the value of the action actually taken next. It became the standard on-policy counterpart to Q-learning.

title: Randomised double-blind comparison of chimeric monoclonal antibody to tumour necrosis factor alpha (cA2) versus placebo in rheumatoid arthritis
authors: Elliott MJ, Maini RN, Feldmann M, Kalden JR, Antoni C, Smolen JS, et al.
summary: Controlled trial showing anti-TNF antibody (infliximab) treats rheumatoid arthritis, validating cytokine blockade and launching the anti-TNF biologic class.

title: A large-scale experiment to assess protein structure prediction methods
authors: Moult J, Pedersen JT, Judson R, Fidelis K
summary: Launched CASP, the blind biennial assessment of structure prediction that defined progress in the field and later certified AlphaFold.

title: Quantitative monitoring of gene expression patterns with a complementary DNA microarray
authors: Schena M, Shalon D, Davis RW, Brown PO
summary: Spotted cDNA microarrays with two-colour fluorescence for parallel gene expression measurement, launching transcriptomics.

title: Serial analysis of gene expression
authors: Velculescu VE, Zhang L, Vogelstein B, Kinzler KW
summary: SAGE: counting concatenated short cDNA tags by sequencing to quantify transcript abundance, a precursor of tag-based RNA-seq.

title: Whole-genome random sequencing and assembly of Haemophilus influenzae Rd
authors: Fleischmann RD, Adams MD, White O, Clayton RA, Kirkness EF, Kerlavage AR, et al.
summary: First genome of a free-living organism, sequenced by whole-genome shotgun, proving the strategy for large genomes.

title: Improved Backing-off for M-gram Language Modeling
authors: Kneser R, Ney H
summary: Introduced Kneser-Ney smoothing, which uses continuation counts for lower-order distributions and became the best-performing n-gram smoothing method.

title: Temporal Difference Learning and TD-Gammon
authors: Tesauro G
summary: A neural network trained by TD(lambda) self-play reached world-class backgammon play and found new strategies that human experts adopted. It was the first major success of RL with neural function approximation.

title: T lymphocyte-directed gene therapy for ADA- SCID: initial trial results after 4 years
authors: Blaese RM, Culver KW, Miller AD, Carter CS, Fleisher T, Clerici M, et al.
summary: Report of the first approved human gene therapy trial (begun 1990 with Ashanti DeSilva), using retrovirally transduced T cells to treat ADA deficiency.

title: Three-Dimensional Electron Microscopy of Macromolecular Assemblies
authors: Frank J
summary: Codified single-particle reconstruction, the image-processing framework (alignment, classification, 3D reconstruction) developed by Frank and used by all single-particle cryo-EM (Nobel 2017).

title: Characterization of individual polynucleotide molecules using a membrane channel
authors: Kasianowicz JJ, Brandin E, Branton D, Deamer DW
summary: Showed single-stranded nucleic acids translocating through an alpha-hemolysin pore produce measurable current blockades, founding nanopore sequencing.

title: Life with 6000 genes
authors: Goffeau A, Barrell BG, Bussey H, Davis RW, Dujon B, Feldmann H, et al.
summary: Complete genome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the first eukaryotic genome.

title: The future of genetic studies of complex human diseases
authors: Risch N, Merikangas K
summary: Argued genome-wide association would be far more powerful than linkage for common complex-disease alleles.

title: Hybrid restriction enzymes: zinc finger fusions to Fok I cleavage domain
authors: Kim YG, Cha J, Chandrasegaran S
summary: Fused programmable zinc-finger DNA-binding domains to a nuclease domain, creating the first designer nucleases (ZFNs).

title: Neuro-Dynamic Programming
authors: Bertsekas DP, Tsitsiklis JN
summary: Rigorous treatment of approximate dynamic programming and RL with function approximation. It put TD learning and Q-learning on solid theoretical ground.

title: Enhancement of antitumor immunity by CTLA-4 blockade
authors: Leach DR, Krummel MF, Allison JP
summary: Antibody blockade of the CTLA-4 checkpoint caused tumor rejection in mice, the founding experiment of checkpoint immunotherapy (Nobel 2018).

title: In vivo gene delivery and stable transduction of nondividing cells by a lentiviral vector
authors: Naldini L, Blömer U, Gallay P, Ory D, Mulligan R, Gage FH, et al.
summary: Developed HIV-derived lentiviral vectors that transduce non-dividing cells, now standard for ex vivo HSC gene therapy and CAR-T manufacturing.

title: Assembly of protein tertiary structures from fragments with similar local sequences using simulated annealing and Bayesian scoring functions
authors: Simons KT, Kooperberg C, Huang E, Baker D
summary: Introduced Rosetta fragment-assembly de novo structure prediction, the basis of the Rosetta suite for both prediction and design.

title: De novo protein design: fully automated sequence selection
authors: Dahiyat BI, Mayo SL
summary: The first fully computationally designed sequence for a protein fold (a zinc-finger fold), validating physics-based automated design.

title: Gapped BLAST and PSI-BLAST: a new generation of protein database search programs
authors: Altschul SF, Madden TL, Schäffer AA, Zhang J, Zhang Z, Miller W, et al.
summary: Added gapped alignment and iterative position-specific scoring (PSI-BLAST) to BLAST, greatly improving remote homology detection and supplying profiles to structure predictors.

title: Pfam: a comprehensive database of protein domain families based on seed alignments
authors: Sonnhammer EL, Eddy SR, Durbin R
summary: Created Pfam, the curated database of protein domain families represented as profile HMMs, a standard resource for annotation and later for MSA-based structure prediction.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
authors: Hochreiter S, Schmidhuber J
summary: Introduced the LSTM cell with gated constant-error carousels that overcome vanishing gradients, dominating sequence modeling for two decades.

title: Neandertal DNA sequences and the origin of modern humans
authors: Krings M, Stone A, Schmitz RW, Krainitzki H, Stoneking M, Pääbo S
summary: First Neanderthal mitochondrial DNA sequence from the type specimen, launching ancient human DNA research.

title: Presence of fetal DNA in maternal plasma and serum
authors: Lo YMD, Corbetta N, Chamberlain PF, Rai V, Sargent IL, Redman CW, et al.
summary: Discovered cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma, founding non-invasive prenatal testing and cfDNA diagnostics.

title: Viable offspring derived from fetal and adult mammalian cells
authors: Wilmut I, Schnieke AE, McWhir J, Kind AJ, Campbell KHS
summary: Cloning of Dolly the sheep by somatic cell nuclear transfer, proving adult nuclei can be reprogrammed to totipotency.

title: Automated docking using a Lamarckian genetic algorithm and an empirical binding free energy function
authors: Morris GM, Goodsell DS, Halliday RS, Huey R, Hart WE, Belew RK, et al.
summary: AutoDock 3 introduced a Lamarckian genetic algorithm and empirical free-energy scoring, becoming a widely used docking tool.

title: Profile hidden Markov models
authors: Eddy SR
summary: Reviewed and popularized profile HMMs and the HMMER software for sensitive protein family search.

title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
authors: LeCun Y, Bottou L, Bengio Y, Haffner P
summary: Presented LeNet-5 and the MNIST benchmark, and graph transformer networks for deployed check reading.

title: Efficient BackProp
authors: LeCun Y, Bottou L, Orr GB, Müller KR
venue: Neural Networks: Tricks of the Trade, Springer LNCS 1524
summary: Collected practical recipes for training networks: input normalization, weight initialization, sigmoid choice and learning-rate selection.

title: A sequencing method based on real-time pyrophosphate
authors: Ronaghi M, Uhlén M, Nyrén P
summary: Pyrosequencing: luminescent detection of pyrophosphate released during nucleotide incorporation, the chemistry later scaled by 454.

title: Genome sequence of the nematode C. elegans: a platform for investigating biology
authors: The C. elegans Sequencing Consortium
summary: First genome of a multicellular animal, produced by clone-by-clone sequencing.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
authors: Sutton RS, Barto AG
summary: The standard textbook that unified dynamic programming, Monte Carlo and TD methods into a single framework. It defined the field's vocabulary and trained generations of researchers.

title: Embryonic stem cell lines derived from human blastocysts
authors: Thomson JA, Itskovitz-Eldor J, Shapiro SS, Waknitz MA, Swiergiel JJ, Marshall VS, et al.
summary: First human embryonic stem cell lines, opening human regenerative medicine and disease modeling.

title: Potent and specific genetic interference by double-stranded RNA in Caenorhabditis elegans
authors: Fire A, Xu S, Montgomery MK, Kostas SA, Driver SE, Mello CC
summary: Discovered RNA interference triggered by double-stranded RNA (Nobel 2006).

title: Rituximab chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy for relapsed indolent lymphoma: half of patients respond to a four-dose treatment program
authors: McLaughlin P, Grillo-López AJ, Link BK, Levy R, Czuczman MS, Williams ME, et al.
summary: Pivotal trial of rituximab, the first monoclonal antibody approved for cancer (1997), transforming lymphoma treatment.

title: 'Metabonomics': understanding the metabolic responses of living systems to pathophysiological stimuli via multivariate statistical analysis of biological NMR spectroscopic data
authors: Nicholson JK, Lindon JC, Holmes E
summary: Defined metabonomics: NMR-based multivariate profiling of systemic metabolic responses.

title: Quantitative analysis of complex protein mixtures using isotope-coded affinity tags
authors: Gygi SP, Rist B, Gerber SA, Turecek F, Gelb MH, Aebersold R
summary: ICAT stable-isotope labelling for relative quantification by mass spectrometry.

title: Between MDPs and Semi-MDPs: A Framework for Temporal Abstraction in Reinforcement Learning
authors: Sutton RS, Precup D, Singh S
summary: Introduced the options framework, which models temporally extended actions as semi-Markov decision processes. It became the standard formalism of hierarchical RL.

title: The Protein Data Bank
authors: Berman HM, Westbrook J, Feng Z, Gilliland G, Bhat TN, Weissig H, et al.
summary: Described the modernized RCSB Protein Data Bank, the curated archive of experimental structures whose ~200,000 entries trained AlphaFold and successors.

title: The large-scale organization of metabolic networks
authors: Jeong H, Tombor B, Albert R, Oltvai ZN, Barabási AL
summary: Found scale-free topology across metabolic networks of 43 organisms, catalyzing network biology.

title: Bundle Adjustment - A Modern Synthesis
authors: Triggs B, McLauchlan PF, Hartley RI, Fitzgibbon AW
venue: Vision Algorithms: Theory and Practice, LNCS 1883
summary: Comprehensive treatment of sparse nonlinear least-squares refinement of cameras and 3D points, the backbone of SfM and SLAM.

title: Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision
authors: Hartley R, Zisserman A
summary: The standard reference on projective geometry, epipolar geometry, the fundamental matrix, and multi-view reconstruction.

title: Normalized Cuts and Image Segmentation
authors: Shi J, Malik J
summary: Formulated segmentation as normalized graph partitioning solved via spectral relaxation; a cornerstone of grouping-based segmentation.

title: A whole-genome assembly of Drosophila
authors: Myers EW, Sutton GG, Delcher AL, Dew IM, Fasulo DP, Flanigan MJ, et al.
summary: The Celera overlap-layout-consensus assembler that showed WGS could assemble a complex eukaryotic genome.

title: Analysis of the genome sequence of the flowering plant Arabidopsis thaliana
authors: The Arabidopsis Genome Initiative
summary: First plant genome, the model Arabidopsis thaliana.

title: Electrostatic axially harmonic orbital trapping: a high-performance technique of mass analysis
authors: Makarov A
summary: The Orbitrap mass analyser, delivering high resolution and accuracy that came to dominate proteomics.

title: Genome-wide location and function of DNA binding proteins
authors: Ren B, Robert F, Wyrick JJ, Aparicio O, Jennings EG, Simon I, et al.
summary: ChIP-chip: chromatin immunoprecipitation combined with microarrays to map transcription-factor binding genome-wide.

title: The genome sequence of Drosophila melanogaster
authors: Adams MD, Celniker SE, Holt RA, Evans CA, Gocayne JD, Amanatides PG, et al.
summary: Fly genome assembled by whole-genome shotgun at Celera, a pilot for the human WGS effort.

title: A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators
authors: Elowitz MB, Leibler S
summary: The repressilator, a three-repressor ring that oscillates in single cells, showing that dynamic behaviour can be designed from parts.

title: Construction of a genetic toggle switch in Escherichia coli
authors: Gardner TS, Cantor CR, Collins JJ
summary: Built a bistable genetic switch from mutually repressing promoters, the first designed, model-driven synthetic gene circuit.

title: Engineering the provitamin A (beta-carotene) biosynthetic pathway into (carotenoid-free) rice endosperm
authors: Ye X, Al-Babili S, Klöti A, Zhang J, Lucca P, Beyer P, et al.
summary: Golden Rice: a multi-gene carotenoid pathway installed in rice endosperm, the flagship nutritional-biofortification transgenic crop.

title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ng AY, Russell S
summary: Formalized inverse reinforcement learning, which recovers a reward function that explains observed optimal behavior, and gave linear-programming algorithms for it. It opened the field of learning rewards from demonstrations.

title: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation
authors: Sutton RS, McAllester D, Singh S, Mansour Y
venue: NIPS 1999 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 12)
summary: Proved the policy gradient theorem, which writes the gradient of performance in terms of action values without differentiating the state distribution. It also showed convergence with compatible function approximation and grounded modern actor-critic methods.

title: Gene therapy of human severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)-X1 disease
authors: Cavazzana-Calvo M, Hacein-Bey S, de Saint Basile G, Gross F, Yvon E, Nusbaum P, et al.
summary: First clear clinical success of gene therapy: retrovirally corrected stem cells restored immunity in X-SCID infants.

title: Islet transplantation in seven patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus using a glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive regimen
authors: Shapiro AMJ, Lakey JRT, Ryan EA, Korbutt GS, Toth E, Warnock GL, et al.
summary: The Edmonton protocol achieved insulin independence via donor islet infusion, proving cell replacement could treat type 1 diabetes.

title: An Eulerian path approach to DNA fragment assembly
authors: Pevzner PA, Tang H, Waterman MS
summary: Recast genome assembly as finding Eulerian paths in a de Bruijn graph, the paradigm adopted by short-read assemblers.

title: Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features
authors: Viola P, Jones M
summary: Real-time face detection using Haar-like features, integral images, AdaBoost and an attentional cascade; the first practical real-time detector.

title: Initial sequencing and analysis of the human genome
authors: Lander ES, Linton LM, Birren B, Nusbaum C, Zody MC, Baldwin J, et al.
summary: Public Human Genome Project draft sequence from hierarchical clone-based shotgun sequencing.

title: Large-scale analysis of the yeast proteome by multidimensional protein identification technology
authors: Washburn MP, Wolters D, Yates JR
summary: MudPIT: multidimensional LC-MS/MS identifying ~1,500 yeast proteins without gels.

title: The sequence of the human genome
authors: Venter JC, Adams MD, Myers EW, Li PW, Mural RJ, Sutton GG, et al.
summary: Celera's whole-genome shotgun draft of the human genome, published alongside the public draft.

title: Expanding the genetic code of Escherichia coli
authors: Wang L, Brock A, Herrick B, Schultz PG
summary: An orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pair let living bacteria incorporate an unnatural amino acid in response to a reassigned codon.

title: Conditional Random Fields: Probabilistic Models for Segmenting and Labeling Sequence Data
authors: Lafferty J, McCallum A, Pereira F
summary: Introduced CRFs, globally normalized discriminative sequence models that avoid label bias and dominated tagging and NER before neural methods.

title: Duplexes of 21-nucleotide RNAs mediate RNA interference in cultured mammalian cells
authors: Elbashir SM, Harborth J, Lendeckel W, Yalcin A, Weber K, Tuschl T
summary: Synthetic siRNAs silence genes in mammalian cells without the interferon response, enabling RNAi therapeutics.

title: Use of chemotherapy plus a monoclonal antibody against HER2 for metastatic breast cancer that overexpresses HER2
authors: Slamon DJ, Leyland-Jones B, Shak S, Fuchs H, Paton V, Bajamonde A, et al.
summary: Phase 3 trial showing humanized anti-HER2 trastuzumab improves survival, a landmark for biomarker-targeted antibody therapy.

title: Systems biology: a brief overview
authors: Kitano H
summary: Influential manifesto defining systems biology as system-level understanding through structure, dynamics, control and design.

title: Training Products of Experts by Minimizing Contrastive Divergence
authors: Hinton GE
summary: Introduced contrastive divergence, an efficient approximate learning rule that made training restricted Boltzmann machines practical.

title: Capturing chromosome conformation
authors: Dekker J, Rippe K, Dekker M, Kleckner N
summary: Chromosome conformation capture (3C), measuring physical contacts between genomic loci by proximity ligation.

title: Metabolomics - the link between genotypes and phenotypes
authors: Fiehn O
summary: Influential framing of mass-spectrometry metabolomics as the phenotypic layer linking genotype to phenotype.

title: Stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture, SILAC, as a simple and accurate approach to expression proteomics
authors: Ong SE, Blagoev B, Kratchmarova I, Kristensen DB, Steen H, Pandey A, et al.
summary: SILAC metabolic labelling for accurate MS-based quantitative proteomics.

title: Identification of genes that are associated with DNA repeats in prokaryotes
authors: Jansen R, van Embden JDA, Gaastra W, Schouls LM
summary: Named CRISPR and the associated cas genes, recognising the repeat family as a coherent, widespread prokaryotic system.

title: BLEU: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation
authors: Papineni K, Roukos S, Ward T, Zhu WJ
summary: Proposed BLEU, an n-gram precision metric with a brevity penalty that became the standard automatic MT evaluation measure.

title: A Natural Policy Gradient
authors: Kakade S
venue: NIPS 2001 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 14)
summary: Proposed following the natural gradient, preconditioned by the Fisher information of the policy, so updates do not depend on how the policy is parameterized. It inspired natural actor-critic and TRPO.

title: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem
authors: Auer P, Cesa-Bianchi N, Fischer P
summary: Introduced UCB1 and proved logarithmic regret bounds that hold for any finite time, not just asymptotically. Optimism in the face of uncertainty became a key principle of exploration, used in UCT and MCTS.

title: Near-Optimal Reinforcement Learning in Polynomial Time
authors: Kearns M, Singh S
summary: The E3 algorithm was the first to prove that near-optimal behavior in general MDPs can be learned in polynomial time, by explicitly balancing exploration and exploitation.

title: R-max - A General Polynomial Time Algorithm for Near-Optimal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Brafman RI, Tennenholtz M
summary: R-max treats unknown states as maximally rewarding, giving a simple optimistic model-based algorithm with polynomial sample complexity. It also extends to stochastic games.

title: Approval of adalimumab (Humira), the first fully human therapeutic monoclonal antibody
authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Abbott Laboratories
summary: Adalimumab, derived by phage display, became the first fully human mAb approved and later the world's best-selling drug.

title: Novel adeno-associated viruses from rhesus monkeys as vectors for human gene therapy
authors: Gao GP, Alvira MR, Wang L, Calcedo R, Johnston J, Wilson JM
summary: Discovered AAV7 and AAV8 serotypes with improved tissue tropism, expanding the AAV vector toolkit used in liver and muscle gene therapies.

title: Design of a novel globular protein fold with atomic-level accuracy
authors: Kuhlman B, Dantas G, Ireton GC, Varani G, Stoddard BL, Baker D
summary: Designed Top7, a protein with a fold not seen in nature, whose crystal structure matched the Rosetta model with atomic accuracy.

title: The systems biology markup language (SBML): a medium for representation and exchange of biochemical network models
authors: Hucka M, Finney A, Sauro HM, Bolouri H, Doyle JC, Kitano H, et al.
summary: Defined SBML, the standard exchange format for biochemical network models.

title: Video Google: A Text Retrieval Approach to Object Matching in Videos
authors: Sivic J, Zisserman A
summary: Quantized local descriptors into 'visual words' for inverted-file retrieval, establishing the bag-of-visual-words paradigm.

title: Tandem mass tags: a novel quantification strategy for comparative analysis of complex protein mixtures by MS/MS
authors: Thompson A, Schäfer J, Kuhn K, Kienle S, Schwarz J, Schmidt G, et al.
summary: Isobaric tandem mass tags allowing multiplexed peptide quantification.

title: Idempotent vector design for standard assembly of BioBricks
authors: Knight TF
venue: MIT Synthetic Biology Working Group Technical Report
summary: Defined the BioBrick standard prefix/suffix assembly scheme, introducing interchangeable parts and engineering abstraction to biology.

title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
authors: Bengio Y, Ducharme R, Vincent P, Jauvin C
summary: Jointly learned distributed word embeddings and a neural network n-gram language model, beating smoothed n-grams and founding neural language modeling.

title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation
authors: Blei DM, Ng AY, Jordan MI
summary: Bayesian generative topic model representing documents as mixtures of topics, the standard tool for unsupervised text exploration.

title: Statistical Phrase-Based Translation
authors: Koehn P, Och FJ, Marcu D
summary: Phrase-based SMT translating multi-word segments, which became the dominant MT paradigm until neural MT.

title: Development of potent monoclonal antibody auristatin conjugates for cancer therapy
authors: Doronina SO, Toki BE, Torgov MY, Mendelsohn BA, Cerveny CG, Chace DF, et al.
summary: Developed MMAE auristatin linker-payload chemistry that underpins many antibody-drug conjugates, including brentuximab vedotin.

title: Fatal systemic inflammatory response syndrome in a ornithine transcarbamylase deficient patient following adenoviral gene transfer
authors: Raper SE, Chirmule N, Lee FS, Wivel NA, Bagg A, Gao GP, et al.
summary: Analysis of the 1999 death of Jesse Gelsinger after adenoviral vector infusion, which reshaped gene therapy safety oversight.

title: LMO2-associated clonal T cell proliferation in two patients after gene therapy for SCID-X1
authors: Hacein-Bey-Abina S, von Kalle C, Schmidt M, McCormack MP, Wulffraat N, Leboulch P, et al.
summary: Revealed insertional oncogenesis by gamma-retroviral vectors, driving the shift to self-inactivating and lentiviral vectors.

title: Distinctive Image Features from Scale-Invariant Keypoints
authors: Lowe DG
summary: SIFT: scale-space keypoint detection with gradient-histogram descriptors invariant to scale and rotation; dominated matching, recognition and SfM for a decade.

title: Learning Generative Visual Models from Few Training Examples: An Incremental Bayesian Approach Tested on 101 Object Categories
authors: Fei-Fei L, Fergus R, Perona P
venue: CVPR Workshop on Generative-Model Based Vision 2004
summary: Introduced Caltech-101, an early multi-category object recognition benchmark.

title: GPU Implementation of Neural Networks
authors: Oh KS, Jung K
summary: Early demonstration of accelerating neural-network inference on graphics hardware.

title: Finishing the euchromatic sequence of the human genome
authors: International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium
summary: Essentially finished human euchromatic sequence (99% coverage, ~1 error per 100 kb), revising the gene count to ~20,000-25,000.

title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
authors: Abbeel P, Ng AY
summary: Matches the expert's feature expectations by iteratively inferring rewards, with guarantees that the learned policy performs close to the expert. It was applied to driving and later helicopter control.

title: Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection
authors: Dalal N, Triggs B
summary: HOG descriptors with a linear SVM for pedestrian detection; the dominant hand-crafted detection feature before deep learning.

title: A haplotype map of the human genome
authors: International HapMap Consortium
summary: Genotyped over one million SNPs in four populations to chart linkage disequilibrium, enabling tag-SNP GWAS design.

title: Accurate multiplex polony sequencing of an evolved bacterial genome
authors: Shendure J, Porreca GJ, Reppas NB, Lin X, McCutcheon JP, Rosenbaum AM, et al.
summary: Polony sequencing-by-ligation on bead arrays with off-the-shelf instrumentation; a key open-source demonstration of cyclic-array sequencing.

title: Complement factor H polymorphism in age-related macular degeneration
authors: Klein RJ, Zeiss C, Chew EY, Tsai JY, Sackler RS, Haynes C, et al.
summary: First successful genome-wide association study, finding a CFH variant strongly associated with AMD.

title: Genome sequencing in microfabricated high-density picolitre reactors
authors: Margulies M, Egholm M, Altman WE, Attiya S, Bader JS, Bemben LA, et al.
summary: 454 emulsion-PCR pyrosequencing in picolitre wells: the first commercial massively parallel next-generation sequencing platform.

title: Highly efficient endogenous human gene correction using designed zinc-finger nucleases
authors: Urnov FD, Miller JC, Lee YL, Beausejour CM, Rock JM, Augustus S, et al.
summary: Efficient correction of an endogenous human disease gene in cultured cells, showing therapeutic genome editing was feasible.

title: Intervening sequences of regularly spaced prokaryotic repeats derive from foreign genetic elements
authors: Mojica FJM, Díez-Villaseñor C, García-Martínez J, Soria E
summary: Found that CRISPR spacers match phage and plasmid sequences, and proposed CRISPR is a prokaryotic adaptive immune system.

title: Neural Fitted Q Iteration - First Experiences with a Data Efficient Neural Reinforcement Learning Method
authors: Riedmiller M
