summary: Used a multilayer perceptron as the regressor in fitted Q iteration, retraining it on all stored transitions. A direct precursor of DQN's experience replay and neural Q-learning.

title: Tree-Based Batch Mode Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ernst D, Geurts P, Wehenkel L
summary: Introduced fitted Q iteration, which repeatedly fits a regressor (tree ensembles) to Bellman targets computed from a fixed batch of transitions. A foundation of batch and offline RL.

title: Suppression of RNA recognition by Toll-like receptors: the impact of nucleoside modification and the evolutionary origin of RNA
authors: Karikó K, Buckstein M, Ni H, Weissman D
summary: Showed modified nucleosides (e.g. pseudouridine) let mRNA evade innate immune sensing, the key enabler of mRNA vaccines (Nobel 2023).

title: An Introduction to Systems Biology: Design Principles of Biological Circuits
authors: Alon U
summary: Textbook framing gene circuits through network motifs, robustness and optimal design.

title: Photo Tourism: Exploring Photo Collections in 3D
authors: Snavely N, Seitz SM, Szeliski R
summary: Large-scale structure from motion on unordered Internet photos (Bundler), enabling 3D browsing of tourist sites.

title: SURF: Speeded Up Robust Features
authors: Bay H, Tuytelaars T, Van Gool L
summary: Fast scale- and rotation-invariant detector/descriptor using integral images and box-filter Hessian approximations.

title: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets
authors: Hinton GE, Osindero S, Teh YW
summary: Showed deep belief networks can be trained greedily layer by layer as stacked RBMs, sparking the deep-learning renaissance.

title: Reducing the Dimensionality of Data with Neural Networks
authors: Hinton GE, Salakhutdinov RR
summary: Used RBM pretraining to train deep autoencoders that learn low-dimensional codes far better than PCA.

title: Production of the antimalarial drug precursor artemisinic acid in engineered yeast
authors: Ro DK, Paradise EM, Ouellet M, Fisher KJ, Newman KL, Ndungu JM, et al.
summary: Rebuilt a plant terpenoid pathway in yeast to make artemisinic acid, the landmark demonstration of metabolic engineering for a drug.

title: Bandit Based Monte-Carlo Planning
authors: Kocsis L, Szepesvari C
summary: Introduced UCT, which applies the UCB1 bandit rule at each node of a Monte Carlo search tree and proved its consistency. UCT became the core of Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS).

title: Efficient Selectivity and Backup Operators in Monte-Carlo Tree Search
authors: Coulom R
summary: Coined Monte Carlo tree search and combined random rollouts with selective tree growth in the Go program Crazy Stone. MCTS transformed computer Go and later underpinned AlphaGo.

title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from mouse embryonic and adult fibroblast cultures by defined factors
authors: Takahashi K, Yamanaka S
summary: Four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) reprogram fibroblasts into induced pluripotent stem cells (Nobel 2012).

title: MonoSLAM: Real-Time Single Camera SLAM
authors: Davison AJ, Reid ID, Molton ND, Stasse O
summary: Real-time monocular simultaneous localization and mapping with an EKF over sparse features.

title: Genome-wide association study of 14,000 cases of seven common diseases and 3,000 shared controls
authors: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
summary: Landmark GWAS establishing design and QC standards and identifying 24 loci across seven common diseases.

title: Genome-wide mapping of in vivo protein-DNA interactions
authors: Johnson DS, Mortazavi A, Myers RM, Wold B
summary: ChIP-seq: sequencing immunoprecipitated DNA to map transcription-factor (NRSF) binding at high resolution genome-wide.

title: Identification and analysis of functional elements in 1% of the human genome by the ENCODE pilot project
authors: ENCODE Project Consortium
summary: ENCODE pilot: integrated maps of transcription, chromatin and binding over 1% of the genome, revealing pervasive transcription.

title: The Human Microbiome Project
authors: Turnbaugh PJ, Ley RE, Hamady M, Fraser-Liggett CM, Knight R, Gordon JI
summary: Outlined the Human Microbiome Project to characterise microbial communities of the human body by metagenomics.

title: CRISPR provides acquired resistance against viruses in prokaryotes
authors: Barrangou R, Fremaux C, Deveau H, Richards M, Boyaval P, Moineau S, et al.
summary: Experimental proof that spacer acquisition confers heritable, sequence-specific phage resistance requiring cas genes.

title: Regret Minimization in Games with Incomplete Information
authors: Zinkevich M, Johanson M, Bowling M, Piccione C
venue: NIPS 2007 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 20)
summary: Introduced counterfactual regret minimization (CFR), which converges to Nash equilibria in large extensive-form imperfect-information games. It underpins the poker breakthroughs DeepStack, Libratus and Pluribus.

title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from adult human fibroblasts by defined factors
authors: Takahashi K, Tanabe K, Ohnuki M, Narita M, Ichisaka T, Tomoda K, et al.
summary: Generated human iPSCs, providing patient-specific pluripotent cells without embryos.

title: Quadrivalent vaccine against human papillomavirus to prevent high-grade cervical lesions
authors: FUTURE II Study Group
summary: Phase 3 efficacy of the quadrivalent HPV VLP vaccine (Gardasil) against cervical precancer, enabling cervical cancer prevention by vaccination.

title: Anton, a special-purpose machine for molecular dynamics simulation
authors: Shaw DE, Deneroff MM, Dror RO, Kuskin JS, Larson RH, Salmon JK, et al.
summary: A purpose-built supercomputer accelerating biomolecular MD by orders of magnitude, opening millisecond timescales.

title: De novo computational design of retro-aldol enzymes
authors: Jiang L, Althoff EA, Clemente FR, Doyle L, Röthlisberger D, Zanghellini A, et al.
summary: Designed active retro-aldolases with multistep mechanisms using Rosetta theozyme placement, a landmark in de novo enzyme design.

title: Kemp elimination catalysts by computational enzyme design
authors: Röthlisberger D, Khersonsky O, Wollacott AM, Jiang L, DeChancie J, Betker J, et al.
summary: Computationally designed enzymes for a reaction with no natural catalyst, later improved by directed evolution.

title: Velvet: algorithms for de novo short read assembly using de Bruijn graphs
authors: Zerbino DR, Birney E
summary: A practical de Bruijn graph assembler for next-generation short reads, enabling de novo assembly of genomes from Illumina data.

title: Extracting and Composing Robust Features with Denoising Autoencoders
authors: Vincent P, Larochelle H, Bengio Y, Manzagol PA
summary: Introduced denoising autoencoders, which learn robust representations by reconstructing clean inputs from corrupted ones; a conceptual ancestor of diffusion and masked modeling.

title: Scalable Parallel Programming with CUDA
authors: Nickolls J, Buck I, Garland M, Skadron K
summary: Described NVIDIA's CUDA model for general-purpose GPU programming, the platform on which deep learning computation was built.

title: Accurate whole human genome sequencing using reversible terminator chemistry
authors: Bentley DR, Balasubramanian S, Swerdlow HP, Smith GP, Milton J, Brown CG, et al.
summary: Solexa/Illumina bridge amplification with reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis; resequenced a human genome and became the dominant short-read platform.

title: Comprehensive genomic characterization defines human glioblastoma genes and core pathways
authors: Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network
summary: First TCGA marker paper, integrating copy number, expression, methylation and sequencing of glioblastomas.

title: DNA sequencing of a cytogenetically normal acute myeloid leukaemia genome
authors: Ley TJ, Mardis ER, Ding L, Fulton B, McLellan MD, Chen K, et al.
summary: First whole cancer genome sequenced against matched normal, using Illumina short reads.

title: High-resolution mapping and characterization of open chromatin across the genome
authors: Boyle AP, Davis S, Shulha HP, Meltzer P, Margulies EH, Weng Z, et al.
summary: DNase-seq genome-wide mapping of DNase I hypersensitive sites (open chromatin).

title: Imaging individual mRNA molecules using multiple singly labeled probes
authors: Raj A, van den Bogaard P, Rifkin SA, van Oudenaarden A, Tyagi S
summary: Single-molecule FISH with many short labelled oligo probes, the foundation for multiplexed imaging transcriptomics.

title: Mapping and quantifying mammalian transcriptomes by RNA-Seq
authors: Mortazavi A, Williams BA, McCue K, Schaeffer L, Wold B
summary: RNA-seq with RPKM quantification of mouse tissue transcriptomes, replacing microarrays for expression profiling.

title: Noninvasive prenatal diagnosis of fetal chromosomal aneuploidy by massively parallel genomic sequencing of DNA in maternal plasma
authors: Chiu RWK, Chan KCA, Gao Y, Lau VYM, Zheng W, Leung TY, et al.
summary: Shotgun counting of maternal plasma DNA to detect fetal trisomy 21, the basis of clinical NIPT.

title: CRISPR interference limits horizontal gene transfer in staphylococci by targeting DNA
authors: Marraffini LA, Sontheimer EJ
summary: Established that CRISPR systems target DNA rather than RNA, a prerequisite for using them as genome-editing tools.

title: Small CRISPR RNAs guide antiviral defense in prokaryotes
authors: Brouns SJJ, Jore MM, Lundgren M, Westra ER, Slijkhuis RJH, Snijders APL, et al.
summary: Showed CRISPR arrays are processed into small guide RNAs that direct Cas protein complexes to invader nucleic acid.

title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ziebart BD, Maas A, Bagnell JA, Dey AK
summary: Resolves the ambiguity of IRL with a maximum-entropy distribution over trajectories, giving a probabilistic and differentiable formulation. It influenced GAIL and maximum-entropy RL such as SAC.

title: Natural Actor-Critic
authors: Peters J, Schaal S
summary: Combined natural policy gradients with compatible-feature critics into an efficient actor-critic algorithm. It was applied to learning motor skills on robots.

title: Incorporation of pseudouridine into mRNA yields superior nonimmunogenic vector with increased translational capacity and biological stability
authors: Karikó K, Muramatsu H, Welsh FA, Ludwig J, Kato H, Akira S, et al.
summary: Pseudouridine-modified mRNA was both less immunogenic and more efficiently translated in vivo.

title: Tumor regression in cancer patients by very low doses of a T cell-engaging antibody
authors: Bargou R, Leo E, Zugmaier G, Klinger M, Goebeler M, Knop S, et al.
summary: Clinical proof that the CD19xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager blinatumomab redirects T cells to kill lymphoma, establishing the BiTE class.

title: Ultrafast and memory-efficient alignment of short DNA sequences to the human genome
authors: Langmead B, Trapnell C, Pop M, Salzberg SL
summary: Introduced Bowtie, a Burrows-Wheeler-indexed short-read aligner that made mapping to the human genome fast on ordinary hardware.

title: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database
authors: Deng J, Dong W, Socher R, Li LJ, Li K, Fei-Fei L
summary: Millions of images organized by WordNet synsets and crowd-labeled; its ILSVRC subset catalyzed the deep learning revolution.

title: Large-scale Deep Unsupervised Learning using Graphics Processors
authors: Raina R, Madhavan A, Ng AY
summary: Showed GPUs speed up training of deep belief nets and sparse coding by up to 70x, pointing the way to GPU-based deep learning.

title: The Graph Neural Network Model
authors: Scarselli F, Gori M, Tsoi AC, Hagenbuchner M, Monfardini G
summary: Full formulation of GNNs as contraction-map message passing over graphs trained by gradient descent; the origin of graph deep learning.

title: Common polygenic variation contributes to risk of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
authors: International Schizophrenia Consortium, Purcell SM, Wray NR, Stone JL, Visscher PM, O'Donovan MC, et al.
summary: Introduced polygenic risk scores built from many sub-threshold GWAS variants.

title: Comprehensive mapping of long-range interactions reveals folding principles of the human genome
authors: Lieberman-Aiden E, van Berkum NL, Williams L, Imakaev M, Ragoczy T, Telling A, et al.
summary: Hi-C: genome-wide proximity ligation sequencing revealing A/B compartments and fractal-globule chromatin folding.

title: Fast and accurate short read alignment with Burrows-Wheeler transform
authors: Li H, Durbin R
summary: BWA: FM-index based alignment of short reads to large genomes, a core tool of NGS analysis pipelines.

title: Human DNA methylomes at base resolution show widespread epigenomic differences
authors: Lister R, Pelizzola M, Dowen RH, Hawkins RD, Hon G, Tonti-Filippini J, et al.
summary: First single-base whole-genome bisulfite methylomes of human cells, revealing non-CG methylation in stem cells.

title: Real-time DNA sequencing from single polymerase molecules
authors: Eid J, Fehr A, Gray J, Luong K, Lyle J, Otto G, et al.
summary: Pacific Biosciences single-molecule real-time (SMRT) sequencing in zero-mode waveguides, enabling long reads.

title: Sequence and structural variation in a human genome uncovered by short-read, massively parallel ligation sequencing using two-base encoding
authors: McKernan KJ, Peckham HE, Costa GL, McLaughlin SF, Fu Y, Tsung EF, et al.
summary: Applied Biosystems SOLiD sequencing-by-ligation with two-base colour encoding to a human genome.

title: Targeted capture and massively parallel sequencing of 12 human exomes
authors: Ng SB, Turner EH, Robertson PD, Flygare SD, Bigham AW, Lee C, et al.
summary: Exome capture sequencing proof of concept, identifying the cause of Freeman-Sheldon syndrome.

title: mRNA-Seq whole-transcriptome analysis of a single cell
authors: Tang F, Barbacioru C, Wang Y, Nordman E, Lee C, Xu N, et al.
summary: First single-cell RNA-seq, profiling the transcriptome of individual mouse blastomeres.

title: Breaking the code of DNA binding specificity of TAL-type III effectors
authors: Boch J, Scholze H, Schornack S, Landgraf A, Hahn S, Kay S, et al.
summary: Independently cracked and experimentally validated the TAL effector recognition code, enabling custom DNA-binding protein design.

title: Enzymatic assembly of DNA molecules up to several hundred kilobases
authors: Gibson DG, Young L, Chuang RY, Venter JC, Hutchison CA 3rd, Smith HO
summary: Gibson assembly: isothermal, scarless one-pot joining of overlapping DNA fragments, now the default method for building large constructs.

title: Precise genome modification in the crop species Zea mays using zinc-finger nucleases
authors: Shukla VK, Doyon Y, Miller JC, DeKelver RC, Moehle EA, Worden SE, et al.
summary: Brought designer-nuclease editing to a major crop, adding targeted trait insertion to random transgene integration.

title: Programming cells by multiplex genome engineering and accelerated evolution
authors: Wang HH, Isaacs FJ, Carr PA, Sun ZZ, Xu G, Forest CR, et al.
summary: MAGE used pools of oligonucleotides to edit many genomic sites simultaneously and iteratively, enabling combinatorial genome-scale optimisation.

title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
authors: Robertson S, Zaragoza H
venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval 3(4):333-389
summary: Definitive account of the probabilistic relevance model and BM25, still the standard sparse retrieval baseline.

title: Single Lgr5 stem cells build crypt-villus structures in vitro without a mesenchymal niche
authors: Sato T, Vries RG, Snippert HJ, van de Wetering M, Barker N, Stange DE, et al.
summary: Grew self-organizing intestinal organoids from single adult stem cells, launching organoid technology for disease modeling and regeneration.

title: Atomic-level characterization of the structural dynamics of proteins
authors: Shaw DE, Maragakis P, Lindorff-Larsen K, Piana S, Dror RO, Eastwood MP, et al.
summary: Millisecond-scale all-atom MD on Anton captured folding and native-state dynamics of small proteins.

title: AutoDock Vina: improving the speed and accuracy of docking with a new scoring function, efficient optimization, and multithreading
authors: Trott O, Olson AJ
summary: A fast, accurate open-source docking program that became the most widely used docking engine.

title: Object Detection with Discriminatively Trained Part-Based Models
authors: Felzenszwalb PF, Girshick RB, McAllester D, Ramanan D
summary: Deformable Part Models: HOG-based root and part filters trained with latent SVM; state of the art on PASCAL VOC before CNNs.

title: The Pascal Visual Object Classes (VOC) Challenge
authors: Everingham M, Van Gool L, Williams CKI, Winn J, Zisserman A
summary: Annual benchmark (2005-2012) for classification, detection and segmentation that standardized mAP evaluation.

title: Rectified Linear Units Improve Restricted Boltzmann Machines
authors: Nair V, Hinton GE
summary: Introduced rectified linear units for RBMs; ReLU became the default activation enabling training of deep networks.

title: Theano: A CPU and GPU Math Compiler in Python
authors: Bergstra J, Breuleux O, Bastien F, Lamblin P, Pascanu R, Desjardins G, et al.
venue: Proceedings of the 9th Python in Science Conference (SciPy 2010)
summary: Pioneered symbolic computation graphs with automatic differentiation compiled to GPU, the template for later deep-learning frameworks.

title: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Deep Feedforward Neural Networks
authors: Glorot X, Bengio Y
summary: Studied activation and gradient statistics in deep nets and proposed normalized (Xavier) initialization, enabling deep training without pretraining.

title: A draft sequence of the Neandertal genome
authors: Green RE, Krause J, Briggs AW, Maricic T, Stenzel U, Kircher M, et al.
summary: First Neanderthal nuclear genome, showing 1-4% Neanderthal ancestry in non-Africans.

title: A map of human genome variation from population-scale sequencing
authors: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium
summary: Pilot of population-scale low-coverage sequencing cataloguing ~15 million variants.

title: Aptamer-based multiplexed proteomic technology for biomarker discovery
authors: Gold L, Ayers D, Bertino J, Bock C, Bock A, Brody EN, et al.
summary: SomaScan: slow off-rate modified aptamers (SOMAmers) measuring >800 plasma proteins, later ~7,000-11,000.

title: Exome sequencing identifies the cause of a mendelian disorder
authors: Ng SB, Buckingham KJ, Lee C, Bigham AW, Tabor HK, Dent KM, et al.
summary: Identified DHODH mutations as the cause of Miller syndrome, the first novel Mendelian gene discovered by exome sequencing.

title: International network of cancer genome projects
authors: International Cancer Genome Consortium
summary: Launched the ICGC to coordinate comprehensive genomic catalogues of 50 cancer types.

title: The Genome Analysis Toolkit: a MapReduce framework for analyzing next-generation DNA sequencing data
authors: McKenna A, Hanna M, Banks E, Sivachenko A, Cibulskis K, Kernytsky A, et al.
summary: GATK, the standard framework for germline and somatic variant calling from NGS data.

title: Transcript assembly and quantification by RNA-Seq reveals unannotated transcripts and isoform switching during cell differentiation
authors: Trapnell C, Williams BA, Pertea G, Mortazavi A, Kwan G, van Baren MJ, et al.
summary: Cufflinks: reference-based transcript assembly and isoform-level abundance estimation from RNA-seq.

title: Biocatalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines from ketones applied to sitagliptin manufacture
authors: Savile CK, Janey JM, Mundorff EC, Moore JC, Tam S, Jarvis WR, et al.
summary: A transaminase evolved far beyond its natural substrate range replaced a metal-catalysed step in a commercial drug process, the showcase of industrial directed evolution.

title: Creation of a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesized genome
authors: Gibson DG, Glass JI, Lartigue C, Noskov VN, Chuang RY, Algire MA, et al.

title: The CRISPR/Cas bacterial immune system cleaves bacteriophage and plasmid DNA
authors: Garneau JE, Dupuis MÈ, Villion M, Romero DA, Barrangou R, Boyaval P, et al.
summary: Showed Cas9 introduces precise double-strand breaks in target DNA in vivo, identifying the enzyme later used for editing.

title: Recurrent Neural Network Based Language Model
authors: Mikolov T, Karafiát M, Burget L, Černocký J, Khudanpur S
summary: Showed recurrent neural language models substantially reduce perplexity and speech recognition error versus n-gram models.

title: Double Q-learning
authors: van Hasselt H
venue: NIPS 2010 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 23)
summary: Showed that Q-learning overestimates action values because it uses the same estimates to select and evaluate actions, and fixed this with two decoupled estimators. The idea was later carried into Double DQN and TD3.

title: Improved survival with ipilimumab in patients with metastatic melanoma
authors: Hodi FS, O'Day SJ, McDermott DF, Weber RW, Sosman JA, Haanen JB, et al.
summary: First therapy to improve overall survival in metastatic melanoma, leading to approval of the first checkpoint inhibitor.

title: Rational design of cationic lipids for siRNA delivery
authors: Semple SC, Akinc A, Chen J, Sandhu AP, Mui BL, Cho CK, et al.
summary: Designed ionizable lipids (DLin-KC2-DMA) for potent lipid nanoparticle delivery, the lineage leading to patisiran and mRNA vaccine LNPs.

title: Protein 3D structure computed from evolutionary sequence variation
authors: Marks DS, Colwell LJ, Sheridan R, Hopf TA, Pagnani A, Zecchina R, et al.
summary: EVfold used global maximum-entropy models of coevolution to infer residue contacts and fold proteins de novo from sequence families alone.

title: Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Online Learning and Stochastic Optimization
authors: Duchi J, Hazan E, Singer Y
summary: Introduced AdaGrad, per-parameter adaptive learning rates from accumulated squared gradients, the ancestor of RMSProp and Adam.

title: An integrated semiconductor device enabling non-optical genome sequencing
authors: Rothberg JM, Hinz W, Rearick TM, Schultz J, Mileski W, Davey M, et al.
summary: Ion Torrent sequencing detecting proton release on CMOS ion-sensitive chips, eliminating optics.

title: A TALE nuclease architecture for efficient genome editing
authors: Miller JC, Tan S, Qiao G, Barlow KA, Wang J, Xia DF, et al.
summary: Built TALE nucleases that edit endogenous human genes efficiently, giving an easier-to-design alternative to ZFNs.

title: A system for the continuous directed evolution of biomolecules
authors: Esvelt KM, Carlson JC, Liu DR
summary: Phage-assisted continuous evolution (PACE) links a desired activity to phage propagation, running hundreds of evolution rounds per week.

title: CRISPR RNA maturation by trans-encoded small RNA and host factor RNase III
authors: Deltcheva E, Chylinski K, Sharma CM, Gonzales K, Chao Y, Pirzada ZA, et al.
summary: Discovered tracrRNA and its role in crRNA maturation, the missing component of the two-RNA Cas9 system.

title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch
authors: Collobert R, Weston J, Bottou L, Karlen M, Kavukcuoglu K, Kuksa P
summary: A unified neural architecture with pretrained word embeddings learned from unlabeled text that matched feature-engineered systems on tagging, chunking, NER and SRL.

title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
authors: Ross S, Gordon GJ, Bagnell JA
summary: DAgger queries the expert on states visited by the learner and aggregates the data, which fixes behavior cloning's compounding errors with no-regret guarantees.

title: PILCO: A Model-Based and Data-Efficient Approach to Policy Search
authors: Deisenroth MP, Rasmussen CE
summary: Learns a Gaussian-process dynamics model and propagates model uncertainty through long-horizon predictions to improve the policy analytically. It learned cart-pole and robot tasks in seconds of real interaction.

title: Adenovirus-associated virus vector-mediated gene transfer in hemophilia B
authors: Nathwani AC, Tuddenham EGD, Rangarajan S, Rosales C, McIntosh J, Linch DC, et al.
summary: Single peripheral infusion of AAV8-factor IX produced durable expression in hemophilia B, a turning point for systemic AAV gene therapy.

title: Chimeric antigen receptor–modified T cells in chronic lymphoid leukemia
authors: Porter DL, Levine BL, Kalos M, Bagg A, June CH
summary: Lentiviral CD19 CAR-T cells with 4-1BB costimulation expanded and induced complete remission in CLL.

title: A whole-cell computational model predicts phenotype from genotype
authors: Karr JR, Sanghvi JC, Macklin DN, Gutschow MV, Jacobs JM, Bolival B Jr, et al.
summary: The first whole-cell model, integrating 28 submodels to simulate the full life cycle of Mycoplasma genitalium.

title: RELION: implementation of a Bayesian approach to cryo-EM structure determination
authors: Scheres SHW
summary: Introduced Bayesian (maximum a posteriori) refinement for single-particle cryo-EM, central to the resolution revolution.

title: Are we ready for Autonomous Driving? The KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite
authors: Geiger A, Lenz P, Urtasun R
summary: Driving benchmark for stereo, optical flow, visual odometry and 3D detection from a sensor-equipped car.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Krizhevsky A, Sutskever I, Hinton GE
summary: AlexNet: a GPU-trained deep CNN with ReLU and dropout that won ILSVRC-2012 by a wide margin, igniting the deep learning era.

title: UCF101: A Dataset of 101 Human Actions Classes From Videos in The Wild
authors: Soomro K, Zamir AR, Shah M
summary: 13K YouTube clips across 101 actions; a standard action recognition benchmark of the early deep era.

title: An integrated encyclopedia of DNA elements in the human genome
authors: ENCODE Project Consortium
summary: ENCODE phase 2: 1,640 datasets across 147 cell types assigning biochemical activity to most of the genome.

title: Full-length mRNA-Seq from single-cell levels of RNA and individual circulating tumor cells
authors: Ramsköld D, Luo S, Wang YC, Li R, Deng Q, Faridani OR, et al.
summary: Smart-seq: template-switching full-length single-cell RNA-seq.

title: Structure, function and diversity of the healthy human microbiome
authors: Human Microbiome Project Consortium
summary: Reference survey of microbial communities across body sites in 242 healthy adults.

title: Targeted data extraction of the MS/MS spectra generated by data-independent acquisition: a new concept for consistent and accurate proteome analysis
authors: Gillet LC, Navarro P, Tate S, Röst H, Selevsek N, Reiter L, et al.
summary: SWATH-MS data-independent acquisition with targeted extraction for reproducible proteome quantification.

title: Topological domains in mammalian genomes identified by analysis of chromatin interactions
authors: Dixon JR, Selvaraj S, Yue F, Kim A, Li Y, Shen Y, et al.
summary: Identified topologically associating domains (TADs) as conserved megabase-scale units of chromatin organisation.

title: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease in adaptive bacterial immunity
authors: Jinek M, Chylinski K, Fonfara I, Hauer M, Doudna JA, Charpentier E
summary: Reconstituted Cas9 cleavage in vitro and showed a single chimeric guide RNA can be programmed to cut any chosen DNA sequence.

title: Cas9-crRNA ribonucleoprotein complex mediates specific DNA cleavage for adaptive immunity in bacteria
authors: Gasiunas G, Barrangou R, Horvath P, Siksnys V
summary: Independently reconstituted programmable Cas9-crRNA cleavage and defined the PAM requirement and cut-site geometry.

title: High-efficiency TALEN-based gene editing produces disease-resistant rice
authors: Li T, Liu B, Spalding MH, Weeks DP, Yang B
summary: TALEN editing of a bacterial-blight susceptibility gene gave disease-resistant rice, an early transgene-free edited crop trait.

title: Trastuzumab emtansine for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer
authors: Verma S, Miles D, Gianni L, Krop IE, Welslau M, Baselga J, et al.
summary: EMILIA trial establishing T-DM1, an antibody-drug conjugate, as superior to standard therapy in HER2+ breast cancer.

title: Electron counting and beam-induced motion correction enable near-atomic-resolution single-particle cryo-EM
authors: Li X, Mooney P, Zheng S, Booth CR, Braunfeld MB, Gubbens S, et al.
summary: Showed that direct electron detectors with motion correction enable near-atomic resolution, a key enabler of the cryo-EM resolution revolution.

title: Structure of the TRPV1 ion channel determined by electron cryo-microscopy
authors: Liao M, Cao E, Julius D, Cheng Y
summary: A 3.4 Å single-particle cryo-EM structure of a membrane protein without crystals, the emblematic result of the resolution revolution.

title: On the Difficulty of Training Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Pascanu R, Mikolov T, Bengio Y
summary: Analyzed exploding/vanishing gradients geometrically and introduced gradient-norm clipping, now standard practice.

title: On the Importance of Initialization and Momentum in Deep Learning
authors: Sutskever I, Martens J, Dahl G, Hinton G
summary: Showed that careful initialization with (Nesterov) momentum SGD can train deep and recurrent networks without pretraining.

title: Signatures of mutational processes in human cancer
authors: Alexandrov LB, Nik-Zainal S, Wedge DC, Aparicio SAJR, Behjati S, Biankin AV, et al.
summary: Extracted 21 mutational signatures from ~7,000 cancers, linking them to processes such as smoking, UV and APOBEC.

title: Smart-seq2 for sensitive full-length transcriptome profiling in single cells
authors: Picelli S, Björklund ÅK, Faridani OR, Sagasser S, Winberg G, Sandberg R
summary: Optimised template-switching chemistry giving sensitive full-length single-cell transcriptomes; a plate-based standard.

title: Transposition of native chromatin for fast and sensitive epigenomic profiling of open chromatin, DNA-binding proteins and nucleosome position
authors: Buenrostro JD, Giresi PG, Zaba LC, Chang HY, Greenleaf WJ
summary: ATAC-seq: Tn5 transposase tagmentation of accessible chromatin, a fast low-input replacement for DNase-seq.

title: High-level semi-synthetic production of the potent antimalarial artemisinin
authors: Paddon CJ, Westfall PJ, Pitera DJ, Benjamin K, Fisher K, McPhee D, et al.
summary: Scaled engineered yeast plus chemical conversion to industrial semi-synthetic artemisinin, the first commercial synthetic-biology drug supply.

title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR/Cas systems
authors: Cong L, Ran FA, Cox D, Lin S, Barretto R, Habib N, et al.
summary: Engineered Cas9 for mammalian cells and showed efficient multiplexed editing of human and mouse genomes.

title: RNA-guided human genome engineering via Cas9
authors: Mali P, Yang L, Esvelt KM, Aach J, Guell M, DiCarlo JE, et al.
summary: Demonstrated RNA-guided editing and homology-directed repair in human cells, including stem cells, with a simple guide-RNA toolkit.

title: Repurposing CRISPR as an RNA-guided platform for sequence-specific control of gene expression
authors: Qi LS, Larson MH, Gilbert LA, Doudna JA, Weissman JS, Arkin AP, et al.
summary: Catalytically dead Cas9 used as a programmable DNA-binding module (CRISPRi), separating targeting from cutting.

title: Targeted genome modification of crops using CRISPR/Cas systems
authors: Shan Q, Wang Y, Li J, Zhang Y, Chen K, Liang Z, et al.
summary: First CRISPR editing in crop plants (rice and wheat), which rapidly became the standard method of plant breeding research.

title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
authors: Mikolov T, Sutskever I, Chen K, Corrado G, Dean J
summary: Added negative sampling, frequent-word subsampling and phrase vectors to skip-gram, making word2vec the standard embedding method.

title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
authors: Mikolov T, Chen K, Corrado G, Dean J
summary: Introduced word2vec (CBOW and skip-gram), cheap log-linear models whose embeddings capture semantic and syntactic analogies at scale.

title: Guided Policy Search
authors: Levine S, Koltun V
summary: Uses trajectory optimization to produce guiding samples that steer the training of complex neural network policies toward high-reward regions. A precursor of end-to-end visuomotor learning.

title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Mnih V, Kavukcuoglu K, Silver D, Graves A, Antonoglou I, Wierstra D, et al.
summary: First deep Q-network: a convolutional network trained with Q-learning and experience replay to play Atari games directly from pixels. It launched the deep RL era.

title: The Arcade Learning Environment: An Evaluation Platform for General Agents
authors: Bellemare MG, Naddaf Y, Veness J, Bowling M
summary: A platform exposing dozens of Atari 2600 games as RL environments with a common interface. It became the main benchmark for deep RL from DQN to Agent57.

title: An erythroid enhancer of BCL11A subject to genetic variation determines fetal hemoglobin level
authors: Bauer DE, Kamran SC, Lessard S, Xu J, Fujiwara Y, Lin C, et al.
summary: Identified the erythroid-specific BCL11A enhancer as a target whose disruption reactivates fetal hemoglobin, the basis of exa-cel.

title: Safety and tumor responses with lambrolizumab (anti-PD-1) in melanoma
authors: Hamid O, Robert C, Daud A, Hodi FS, Hwu WJ, Kefford R, et al.
summary: Early trial of lambrolizumab (pembrolizumab) showing high response rates, leading to the first anti-PD-1 approval (2014).

title: Structure-based design of a fusion glycoprotein vaccine for respiratory syncytial virus
authors: McLellan JS, Chen M, Joyce MG, Sastry M, Stewart-Jones GBE, Yang Y, et al.
summary: Stabilized RSV F in its prefusion conformation (DS-Cav1), demonstrating structure-based vaccine design and paving the way for RSV vaccines.

title: Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2
authors: Love MI, Huber W, Anders S
summary: Introduced DESeq2, a negative-binomial shrinkage method for differential expression analysis that became a standard for RNA-seq.

title: Proof of principle for epitope-focused vaccine design
authors: Correia BE, Bates JT, Loomis RJ, Baneyx G, Carrico C, Jardine JG, et al.
summary: Computationally designed scaffolds presenting an RSV neutralizing epitope that elicited neutralizing antibodies in macaques.

title: The resolution revolution
authors: Kühlbrandt W
summary: Named and documented the 2013-2014 jump of cryo-EM to near-atomic resolution driven by direct detectors and new software.

title: Discriminative Unsupervised Feature Learning with Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Dosovitskiy A, Springenberg JT, Riedmiller M, Brox T
summary: Exemplar CNN: treats each image and its augmentations as a surrogate class, an early instance-discrimination approach to self-supervision.

title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
authors: Lin TY, Maire M, Belongie S, Hays J, Perona P, Ramanan D, et al.
summary: Large-scale dataset with instance segmentation of 80 categories in context plus captions; the primary detection and segmentation benchmark.

title: Rich Feature Hierarchies for Accurate Object Detection and Semantic Segmentation
authors: Girshick R, Donahue J, Darrell T, Malik J
summary: R-CNN: CNN features on region proposals with ImageNet pre-training and fine-tuning, nearly doubling PASCAL VOC mAP.

title: Two-Stream Convolutional Networks for Action Recognition in Videos
authors: Simonyan K, Zisserman A
summary: Separate spatial (RGB) and temporal (optical flow) CNN streams fused for action recognition.

title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
authors: Zeiler MD, Fergus R
summary: ZFNet: deconvolutional visualization of CNN features that guided architecture improvements and won ILSVRC-2013.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
authors: Kingma DP, Welling M
summary: Introduced the variational autoencoder and the reparameterization trick for scalable gradient-based variational inference in deep latent-variable models.

title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
authors: Srivastava N, Hinton G, Krizhevsky A, Sutskever I, Salakhutdinov R
summary: Full treatment of dropout as an efficient approximate ensemble regularizer, a key ingredient of the deep-learning breakthrough.

title: Generative Adversarial Nets
authors: Goodfellow IJ, Pouget-Abadie J, Mirza M, Xu B, Warde-Farley D, Ozair S, et al.
summary: Introduced GANs, training a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game, which led to dramatic advances in image synthesis.

title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
authors: Cho K, van Merriënboer B, Gulcehre C, Bahdanau D, Bougares F, Schwenk H, et al.
summary: Introduced the RNN encoder-decoder and the gated recurrent unit (GRU), a simpler alternative to LSTM.

title: Spectral Networks and Locally Connected Networks on Graphs
authors: Bruna J, Zaremba W, Szlam A, LeCun Y
summary: Generalized convolution to graphs via the graph Laplacian spectrum, founding spectral graph convolutional networks.

title: cuDNN: Efficient Primitives for Deep Learning
authors: Chetlur S, Woolley C, Vandermersch P, Cohen J, Tran J, Catanzaro B, et al.
summary: NVIDIA's library of optimized GPU deep-learning kernels, underpinning nearly all frameworks.

title: A 3D map of the human genome at kilobase resolution reveals principles of chromatin looping
authors: Rao SSP, Huntley MH, Durand NC, Stamenova EK, Bochkov ID, Robinson JT, et al.
summary: In situ Hi-C at kilobase resolution identifying ~10,000 CTCF-anchored loops with convergent motif orientation.

title: A draft map of the human proteome
authors: Kim MS, Pinto SM, Getnet D, Nirujogi RS, Manda SS, Chaerkady R, et al.
summary: MS-based draft human proteome across 30 tissues, published with a parallel ProteomicsDB map (Wilhelm et al.).

title: Homogenous 96-plex PEA immunoassay exhibiting high sensitivity, specificity, and excellent scalability
authors: Assarsson E, Lundberg M, Holmquist G, Björkesten J, Thorsen SB, Ekman D, et al.
summary: Olink proximity extension assay: antibody pairs with DNA reporters read by PCR (later NGS) for multiplexed protein quantification.

title: Massively parallel single-cell RNA-seq for marker-free decomposition of tissues into cell types
authors: Jaitin DA, Kenigsberg E, Keren-Shaul H, Elefant N, Paul F, Zaretsky I, et al.
summary: MARS-seq: automated barcoded 3' single-cell RNA-seq of thousands of immune cells.

title: Single-cell in situ RNA profiling by sequential hybridization
authors: Lubeck E, Coskun AF, Zhiyentayev T, Ahmad M, Cai L
summary: seqFISH: sequential rounds of smFISH barcoding to multiplex transcript detection in situ.

title: A semi-synthetic organism with an expanded genetic alphabet
authors: Malyshev DA, Dhami K, Lavergne T, Chen T, Dai N, Foster JM, et al.
summary: A bacterium stably propagated a third, unnatural base pair in its DNA, extending the chemical alphabet of heredity.

title: Concerning RNA-guided gene drives for the alteration of wild populations
authors: Esvelt KM, Smidler AL, Catteruccia F, Church GM
summary: Proposed CRISPR-based gene drives that spread through wild populations, together with containment strategies and a call for public deliberation.

title: Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening in human cells
authors: Shalem O, Sanjana NE, Hartenian E, Shi X, Scott DA, Mikkelson T, et al.
summary: Pooled genome-wide guide libraries turned editing into a forward-genetic screening platform in human cells.

title: Total synthesis of a functional designer eukaryotic chromosome
authors: Annaluru N, Muller H, Mitchell LA, Ramalingam S, Stracquadanio G, Richardson SM, et al.
summary: synIII, the first synthetic eukaryotic chromosome, redesigned with loxPsym sites for inducible genome scrambling and functional in yeast.

title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
authors: Pennington J, Socher R, Manning CD
summary: Learned word vectors by weighted least-squares factorization of global co-occurrence counts, unifying count-based and predictive embeddings.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
authors: Sutskever I, Vinyals O, Le QV
summary: Showed deep LSTM encoder-decoders map input to output sequences end to end, achieving competitive MT and establishing the seq2seq paradigm.

title: Deterministic Policy Gradient Algorithms
authors: Silver D, Lever G, Heess N, Degris T, Wierstra D, Riedmiller M
summary: Derived the deterministic policy gradient theorem, giving off-policy actor-critic methods for continuous actions that need no integration over the action space. It is the basis of DDPG and TD3.

title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells for sustained remissions in leukemia
authors: Maude SL, Frey N, Shaw PA, Aplenc R, Barrett DM, Bunin NJ, et al.
summary: CTL019 CAR-T achieved 90% complete remission in relapsed ALL, the basis for Kymriah approval.

title: Detection of circulating tumor DNA in early- and late-stage human malignancies
authors: Bettegowda C, Sausen M, Leary RJ, Kinde I, Wang Y, Agrawal N, et al.
summary: Systematic survey of ctDNA across cancers showing liquid biopsy feasibility for detection and monitoring.

title: Generation of functional human pancreatic β cells in vitro
authors: Pagliuca FW, Millman JR, Gürtler M, Segel M, Van Dervort A, Ryu JH, et al.
summary: Scalable differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into glucose-responsive beta cells, the basis of stem-cell islet therapies.

title: Multivalent N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated siRNA localizes in hepatocytes and elicits robust RNAi-mediated gene silencing
authors: Nair JK, Willoughby JLS, Chan A, Charisse K, Alam MR, Wang Q, et al.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society 136:16958–16961
summary: Triantennary GalNAc conjugates deliver subcutaneous siRNA to hepatocytes, the platform behind givosiran, inclisiran and others.

title: Predicting effects of noncoding variants with deep learning-based sequence model
authors: Zhou J, Troyanskaya OG
summary: DeepSEA predicted chromatin features from sequence and scored effects of noncoding variants.

title: Predicting the sequence specificities of DNA- and RNA-binding proteins by deep learning
authors: Alipanahi B, Delong A, Weirauch MT, Frey BJ
summary: DeepBind applied convolutional networks to learn protein-nucleic acid binding specificities, an early landmark of deep learning in genomics.

title: Fast R-CNN
authors: Girshick R
summary: Shared convolutional features with RoI pooling and a multi-task loss, making R-CNN training and inference much faster.

title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
authors: Ren S, He K, Girshick R, Sun J
summary: Region Proposal Network with anchors sharing features with the detector, yielding the canonical two-stage detector.

title: FlowNet: Learning Optical Flow with Convolutional Networks
authors: Dosovitskiy A, Fischer P, Ilg E, Häusser P, Hazırbaş C, Golkov V, et al.
summary: First end-to-end CNN for optical flow estimation, trained on synthetic Flying Chairs data.

title: Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation
authors: Long J, Shelhamer E, Darrell T
summary: Converted classification CNNs into fully convolutional networks with skip-connected upsampling for end-to-end pixelwise prediction.

title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
authors: Szegedy C, Liu W, Jia Y, Sermanet P, Reed S, Anguelov D, et al.
summary: GoogLeNet/Inception: multi-branch Inception modules with 1x1 bottlenecks; won ILSVRC-2014 with high efficiency.

title: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
authors: Russakovsky O, Deng J, Su H, Krause J, Satheesh S, Ma S, et al.
summary: Describes the ILSVRC benchmark (2010-2017) and its role in tracking progress from hand-crafted features to deep CNNs.

title: Learning Spatiotemporal Features with 3D Convolutional Networks
authors: Tran D, Bourdev L, Fergus R, Torresani L, Paluri M
summary: C3D: 3x3x3 convolutions over space-time learn generic video features.

title: ORB-SLAM: A Versatile and Accurate Monocular SLAM System
authors: Mur-Artal R, Montiel JMM, Tardós JD
summary: Feature-based keyframe SLAM with ORB features, loop closing and bundle adjustment; a widely used SLAM baseline.

title: Semantic Image Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Nets and Fully Connected CRFs
authors: Chen LC, Papandreou G, Kokkinos I, Murphy K, Yuille AL
summary: DeepLab: atrous (dilated) convolution plus a dense CRF for sharper semantic segmentation.

title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
authors: Ronneberger O, Fischer P, Brox T
summary: Symmetric encoder-decoder with skip connections trained from few annotated images; dominant in medical imaging and later the standard diffusion denoiser.

title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
authors: Simonyan K, Zisserman A
summary: VGG: showed depth with stacks of 3x3 convolutions improves accuracy; VGG features became a universal backbone.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
authors: Kingma DP, Ba J
summary: Combined momentum with RMSProp-style adaptive scaling and bias correction; became the default optimizer in deep learning.

title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
authors: Ioffe S, Szegedy C
summary: Normalized activations with mini-batch statistics, enabling higher learning rates and much faster, more stable training of deep networks.

title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
authors: Sohl-Dickstein J, Weiss E, Maheswaranathan N, Ganguli S
summary: Introduced diffusion probabilistic models: learn to reverse a gradual noising process, the origin of modern diffusion models.

title: Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification
authors: He K, Zhang X, Ren S, Sun J
summary: Derived variance-preserving (He/Kaiming) initialization for ReLU networks and introduced PReLU.

title: Highway Networks
authors: Srivastava RK, Greff K, Schmidhuber J
summary: Used LSTM-style gates on feedforward skip connections to train networks hundreds of layers deep, anticipating residual networks.

title: NICE: Non-linear Independent Components Estimation
authors: Dinh L, Krueger D, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced invertible additive coupling layers with tractable Jacobians, launching normalizing-flow generative models.

title: Variational Inference with Normalizing Flows
authors: Rezende DJ, Mohamed S
summary: Introduced normalizing flows: chains of invertible transformations that build flexible distributions with tractable densities.

title: A global reference for human genetic variation
authors: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium
summary: Final phase genomes of 2,504 individuals from 26 populations, the standard reference panel for imputation.

title: Droplet barcoding for single-cell transcriptomics applied to embryonic stem cells
authors: Klein AM, Mazutis L, Akartuna I, Tallapragada N, Veres A, Li V, et al.
summary: inDrop: hydrogel-bead droplet barcoding for high-throughput single-cell RNA-seq.

title: Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets
authors: Macosko EZ, Basu A, Satija R, Nemesh J, Shekhar K, Goldman M, et al.
summary: Drop-seq: barcoded beads in nanolitre droplets enabling transcriptomes of tens of thousands of cells.

title: Integrative analysis of 111 reference human epigenomes
authors: Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium, Kundaje A, Meuleman W, Ernst J, Bilenky M, Yen A, et al.
summary: Reference epigenomes for 111 human tissues and cell types, linking chromatin states to disease-associated variants.

title: Spatial reconstruction of single-cell gene expression data
authors: Satija R, Farrell JA, Gennert D, Schier AF, Regev A
summary: Introduced Seurat, inferring spatial origin of single cells; became the leading single-cell analysis toolkit.

title: Spatially resolved, highly multiplexed RNA profiling in single cells
authors: Chen KH, Boettiger AN, Moffitt JR, Wang S, Zhuang X
summary: MERFISH: error-robust combinatorial barcoding imaging of hundreds to thousands of RNA species in single cells.

title: The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) pilot analysis: multitissue gene regulation in humans
authors: GTEx Consortium
summary: Pilot multi-tissue RNA-seq and genotypes from postmortem donors, mapping eQTLs across human tissues.

title: Complete biosynthesis of opioids in yeast
authors: Galanie S, Thodey K, Trenchard IJ, Filsinger Interrante M, Smolke CD
summary: Reconstituted more than twenty plant, mammalian and microbial enzymes in yeast to make opioids from sugar, a benchmark in long-pathway engineering and its governance.

title: Cpf1 is a single RNA-guided endonuclease of a class 2 CRISPR-Cas system
authors: Zetsche B, Gootenberg JS, Abudayyeh OO, Slaymaker IM, Makarova KS, Essletzbichler P, et al.
summary: Characterised Cas12a (Cpf1), a single-RNA-guided nuclease with a different PAM and staggered cuts, broadening the editing toolbox.

title: Epigenome editing by a CRISPR-Cas9-based acetyltransferase activates genes from promoters and enhancers
authors: Hilton IB, D'Ippolito AM, Vockley CM, Thakore PI, Crawford GE, Reddy TE, et al.
summary: Targeted a chromatin-modifying enzyme with dCas9 to switch on endogenous genes, founding programmable epigenome editing.

title: A Large Annotated Corpus for Learning Natural Language Inference
authors: Bowman SR, Angeli G, Potts C, Manning CD
summary: SNLI: 570k human-written premise-hypothesis pairs that made natural language inference a central neural benchmark.

title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
authors: Hinton G, Vinyals O, Dean J
summary: Knowledge distillation: training a small student on a large teacher's softened outputs, widely used to compress language models.

title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
authors: Luong MT, Pham H, Manning CD
summary: Systematized global and local attention with multiplicative scoring, simplifying and improving attentional NMT.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
authors: Bahdanau D, Cho K, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced soft attention letting the decoder align to encoder states, removing the fixed-vector bottleneck; the origin of attention in NLP.

title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
authors: Mnih V, Kavukcuoglu K, Silver D, Rusu AA, Veness J, Bellemare MG, et al.
summary: DQN with experience replay and a target network reached human-level performance on many of 49 Atari games using a single architecture and hyperparameters. It was the landmark demonstration that deep networks and RL could be combined stably.

title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
authors: Schulman J, Levine S, Abbeel P, Jordan MI, Moritz P
summary: TRPO constrains each policy update with a KL-divergence trust region, giving near-monotonic improvement for large neural network policies. It made policy optimization reliable for robotic locomotion and Atari.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: He K, Zhang X, Ren S, Sun J
summary: ResNet: identity skip connections enabled training of 100+ layer networks; won ILSVRC-2015 and became the default backbone across deep learning.

title: Image Style Transfer Using Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Gatys LA, Ecker AS, Bethge M
summary: Neural style transfer: optimizes an image to match CNN content features and Gram-matrix style statistics.

title: SSD: Single Shot MultiBox Detector
authors: Liu W, Anguelov D, Erhan D, Szegedy C, Reed S, Fu CY, Berg AC
summary: Single-stage detector predicting boxes from default anchors on multi-scale feature maps.

title: Structure-from-Motion Revisited
authors: Schönberger JL, Frahm JM
summary: Introduced COLMAP, a robust incremental SfM pipeline that became the default tool for camera pose estimation, including for NeRF data.

title: The Cityscapes Dataset for Semantic Urban Scene Understanding
authors: Cordts M, Omran M, Ramos S, Rehfeld T, Enzweiler M, Benenson R, et al.
summary: High-quality pixel-level annotations of urban street scenes from 50 cities; the standard driving segmentation benchmark.

title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
authors: Redmon J, Divvala S, Girshick R, Farhadi A
summary: YOLO: single-network grid-based regression of boxes and classes, enabling real-time detection and spawning a long model family.

title: Deep Learning
authors: Goodfellow I, Bengio Y, Courville A
summary: The standard textbook consolidating the theory and practice of modern deep learning.

title: Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks
authors: Cohen TS, Welling M
summary: Generalized convolution to symmetry groups beyond translation, founding equivariant deep learning.

title: Layer Normalization
authors: Ba JL, Kiros JR, Hinton GE
summary: Normalized across features within each example instead of across the batch, making normalization usable in RNNs and later standard in Transformers.

title: TensorFlow: A System for Large-Scale Machine Learning
authors: Abadi M, Barham P, Chen J, Chen Z, Davis A, Dean J, et al.
summary: Google's dataflow-graph framework for training and deploying models across heterogeneous devices at scale.

title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Radford A, Metz L, Chintala S
summary: DCGAN: architectural guidelines that made convolutional GANs train stably and revealed meaningful latent-space arithmetic.

title: Analysis of protein-coding genetic variation in 60,706 humans
authors: Lek M, Karczewski KJ, Minikel EV, Samocha KE, Banks E, Fennell T, et al.
summary: ExAC exome aggregation, quantifying gene constraint against loss-of-function variation.

title: Perturb-Seq: dissecting molecular circuits with scalable single-cell RNA profiling of pooled genetic screens
authors: Dixit A, Parnas O, Li B, Chen J, Fulco CP, Jerby-Arnon L, et al.
summary: Combined pooled CRISPR perturbations with droplet single-cell RNA-seq readout.

title: Visualization and analysis of gene expression in tissue sections by spatial transcriptomics
authors: Ståhl PL, Salmén F, Vickovic S, Lundmark A, Navarro JF, Magnusson J, et al.
summary: Spatial Transcriptomics: spatially barcoded oligo-dT arrays capture mRNA from tissue sections, the basis of 10x Visium.

title: Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome
authors: Hutchison CA 3rd, Chuang RY, Noskov VN, Assad-Garcia N, Deerinck TJ, Ellisman MH, et al.
summary: JCVI-syn3.0, a 531 kb designed genome with 473 genes, defining a near-minimal self-replicating cell and exposing many genes of unknown function.

title: Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage
authors: Komor AC, Kim YB, Packer MS, Zuris JA, Liu DR
summary: Fused a cytidine deaminase to dCas9 to convert C to T directly, inventing base editing without double-strand breaks.

title: Rapid, low-cost detection of Zika virus using programmable biomolecular components
authors: Pardee K, Green AA, Takahashi MK, Braff D, Lambert G, Lee JW, et al.
summary: Freeze-dried cell-free gene circuits on paper gave programmable, field-deployable diagnostics, bringing synthetic biology out of the cell.

title: Google's Neural Machine Translation System: Bridging the Gap between Human and Machine Translation
authors: Wu Y, Schuster M, Chen Z, Le QV, Norouzi M, Macherey W, et al.
summary: GNMT: deep LSTM attention model with wordpieces deployed in Google Translate, marking neural MT's production takeover from phrase-based SMT.

title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
authors: Sennrich R, Haddow B, Birch A
summary: Adapted byte-pair encoding for open-vocabulary subword tokenization, now the basis of tokenizers in nearly all LLMs.

title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
authors: Rajpurkar P, Zhang J, Lopyrev K, Liang P
summary: Large extractive reading-comprehension dataset over Wikipedia that drove rapid progress in neural QA and pretrained models.

title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Mnih V, Badia AP, Mirza M, Graves A, Lillicrap TP, Harley T, et al.
summary: Showed that many parallel actor-learners can stabilize deep RL without replay, introducing A3C (asynchronous advantage actor-critic). It trained fast on CPUs and became a widely used baseline.

title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
authors: Lillicrap TP, Hunt JJ, Pritzel A, Heess N, Erez T, Tassa Y, et al.
summary: DDPG combined deterministic policy gradients with DQN's replay buffer and target networks to learn continuous control from states or pixels. A foundational off-policy deep actor-critic.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning
authors: van Hasselt H, Guez A, Silver D
summary: Double DQN uses the online network to select actions and the target network to evaluate them, reducing DQN's overestimation bias and improving Atari scores.

title: Dueling Network Architectures for Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Wang Z, Schaul T, Hessel M, van Hasselt H, Lanctot M, de Freitas N
summary: Splits the Q-network into separate state-value and advantage streams that are combined into Q-values. This lets the agent learn which states matter without having to evaluate every action.

title: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies
authors: Levine S, Finn C, Darrell T, Abbeel P
summary: Trained deep convolutional policies that map raw camera images directly to robot motor torques, using guided policy search. It showed end-to-end deep RL on real robots for manipulation tasks.

title: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
authors: Ho J, Ermon S
summary: GAIL frames imitation as matching occupancy measures with a GAN-style discriminator, learning policies directly without first recovering a reward. It scaled imitation to high-dimensional control.

title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
authors: Schulman J, Moritz P, Levine S, Jordan MI, Abbeel P
summary: Introduced generalized advantage estimation (GAE), an exponentially weighted mix of multi-step TD errors that trades bias against variance. GAE is used in PPO and most on-policy methods.

title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
authors: Silver D, Huang A, Maddison CJ, Guez A, Sifre L, van den Driessche G, et al.
summary: AlphaGo combined policy and value networks, trained by supervised learning from expert games and then by self-play RL, with Monte Carlo tree search. It defeated Fan Hui and then Lee Sedol, reaching a goal long thought to be a decade away.

title: OpenAI Gym
authors: Brockman G, Cheung V, Pettersson L, Schneider J, Schulman J, Tang J, et al.
summary: A toolkit with a common interface to many RL environments, from classic control to Atari and MuJoCo. It became the de facto standard API for benchmarking RL algorithms.

title: Prioritized Experience Replay
authors: Schaul T, Quan J, Antonoglou I, Silver D
summary: Replays transitions in proportion to their TD error, with importance-sampling corrections, so the agent learns more from surprising experience. A standard component of later value-based agents.

title: Unifying Count-Based Exploration and Intrinsic Motivation
authors: Bellemare MG, Srinivasan S, Ostrovski G, Schaul T, Saxton D, Munos R
summary: Derived pseudo-counts from density models so that count-based exploration bonuses work in high-dimensional state spaces. It made major progress on Montezuma's Revenge.

title: Accurate de novo prediction of protein contact map by ultra-deep learning model
authors: Wang S, Sun S, Li Z, Zhang R, Xu J
summary: RaptorX-Contact applied deep residual networks to coevolution features, dramatically improving contact prediction in CASP12.

title: MMseqs2 enables sensitive protein sequence searching for the analysis of massive data sets
authors: Steinegger M, Söding J
summary: A very fast sensitive protein search tool that made searches against billions of sequences practical; later powered ColabFold MSA generation.

title: cryoSPARC: algorithms for rapid unsupervised cryo-EM structure determination
authors: Punjani A, Rubinstein JL, Fleet DJ, Brubaker MA
summary: Introduced stochastic gradient descent ab initio reconstruction and branch-and-bound refinement, making cryo-EM processing fast and accessible.

title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
authors: Huang G, Liu Z, van der Maaten L, Weinberger KQ
summary: DenseNet: connects each layer to all subsequent layers for feature reuse and parameter efficiency.

title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
authors: Lin TY, Dollár P, Girshick R, He K, Hariharan B, Belongie S
summary: Top-down pathway with lateral connections building semantically strong multi-scale features; a standard detection neck.

title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
authors: Lin TY, Goyal P, Girshick R, He K, Dollár P
summary: RetinaNet: focal loss down-weights easy negatives, letting one-stage detectors match two-stage accuracy.

title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks
authors: Isola P, Zhu JY, Zhou T, Efros AA
summary: pix2pix: conditional GAN with U-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator for paired image translation.

title: Mask R-CNN
authors: He K, Gkioxari G, Dollár P, Girshick R
summary: Extended Faster R-CNN with a mask branch and RoIAlign for instance segmentation; ICCV 2017 Marr Prize.

title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
authors: Howard AG, Zhu M, Chen B, Kalenichenko D, Wang W, Weyand T, et al.
summary: Depthwise-separable convolutions with width/resolution multipliers for efficient on-device vision.

title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
authors: Qi CR, Su H, Mo K, Guibas LJ
summary: Permutation-invariant network operating directly on raw point clouds via shared MLPs and symmetric pooling.

title: Quo Vadis, Action Recognition? A New Model and the Kinetics Dataset
authors: Carreira J, Zisserman A
summary: I3D: inflated 2D ImageNet filters into 3D two-stream ConvNets and showed Kinetics pre-training transfers strongly.

title: The Kinetics Human Action Video Dataset
authors: Kay W, Carreira J, Simonyan K, Zhang B, Hillier C, Vijayanarasimhan S, et al.
summary: Large-scale YouTube action dataset (400 classes, later 600/700) that became the ImageNet of video recognition.

title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
authors: Zhu JY, Park T, Isola P, Efros AA
summary: CycleGAN: cycle-consistency loss enabling translation between domains without paired data.

title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
authors: Hestness J, Narang S, Ardalani N, Diamos G, Jun H, Kianinejad H, et al.
summary: Found power-law relationships between generalization error and dataset/model size across domains, prefiguring neural scaling laws.

title: Geometric Deep Learning: Going beyond Euclidean Data
authors: Bronstein MM, Bruna J, LeCun Y, Szlam A, Vandergheynst P
summary: Surveyed and named geometric deep learning: extending neural networks to graphs and manifolds.

title: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit
authors: Jouppi NP, Young C, Patil N, Patterson D, Agrawal G, Bajwa R, et al.
summary: Described Google's TPU, a systolic-array ASIC for neural networks, launching the era of specialized AI accelerators.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
authors: Hamilton WL, Ying R, Leskovec J
summary: GraphSAGE: inductive node embeddings via sampled neighborhood aggregation, scaling GNNs to large evolving graphs.

title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
authors: van den Oord A, Vinyals O, Kavukcuoglu K
summary: Introduced VQ-VAE, learning discrete latent codes via vector quantization, later central to tokenized image and audio generation.

title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
authors: Gilmer J, Schoenholz SS, Riley PF, Vinyals O, Dahl GE
summary: Unified GNN variants as message passing neural networks (MPNNs) and set state of the art on molecular property prediction.

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
authors: Shazeer N, Mirhoseini A, Maziarz K, Davis A, Le Q, Hinton G, et al.
summary: Introduced sparsely-gated MoE layers with thousands of experts, decoupling parameter count from compute and enabling conditional computation at scale.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
authors: Kipf TN, Welling M
summary: Introduced the simple first-order graph convolutional network (GCN), which made GNNs practical and widely adopted.

title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
authors: Zhang C, Bengio S, Hardt M, Recht B, Vinyals O
summary: Showed deep nets can fit random labels, challenging classical capacity-based explanations of generalization.

title: Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Arjovsky M, Chintala S, Bottou L
summary: Reformulated GAN training with the Wasserstein distance, improving stability and providing a meaningful loss.

title: Canu: scalable and accurate long-read assembly via adaptive k-mer weighting and repeat separation
authors: Koren S, Walenz BP, Berlin K, Miller JR, Bergman NH, Phillippy AM
summary: Long-read assembler for noisy PacBio and nanopore reads, descended from the Celera Assembler.

title: Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells
authors: Zheng GXY, Terry JM, Belgrader P, Ryvkin P, Ziraldo SB, Wheeler TD, et al.
summary: 10x Genomics GemCode/Chromium droplet platform profiling ~250,000 cells, the commercial standard for scRNA-seq.

title: Simultaneous epitope and transcriptome measurement in single cells
authors: Stoeckius M, Hafemeister C, Stephenson W, Houck-Loomis B, Chattopadhyay PK, Swerdlow H, et al.
summary: CITE-seq: oligo-barcoded antibodies for joint surface-protein and RNA profiling in single cells.

title: The Human Cell Atlas
authors: Regev A, Teichmann SA, Lander ES, Amit I, Benoist C, Birney E, et al.
summary: White paper launching the Human Cell Atlas to map every human cell type with single-cell and spatial methods.

title: Nucleic acid detection with CRISPR-Cas13a/C2c2
authors: Gootenberg JS, Abudayyeh OO, Lee JW, Essletzbichler P, Dy AJ, Joung J, et al.
summary: SHERLOCK coupled Cas13 collateral cleavage to isothermal amplification for attomolar nucleic acid detection, later used for SARS-CoV-2 tests.

title: Programmable base editing of A·T to G·C in genomic DNA without DNA cleavage
authors: Gaudelli NM, Komor AC, Rees HA, Packer MS, Badran AH, Bryson DI, et al.
summary: Evolved an adenine deaminase that does not exist in nature to make A-to-G base editors, covering the most common pathogenic point mutations.

title: RNA targeting with CRISPR-Cas13a
authors: Abudayyeh OO, Gootenberg JS, Essletzbichler P, Han S, Joung J, Belanto JJ, et al.
summary: Used Cas13 for programmable knockdown and editing of RNA in mammalian cells, extending CRISPR beyond DNA.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Vaswani A, Shazeer N, Parmar N, Uszkoreit J, Jones L, Gomez AN, et al.
summary: Introduced the Transformer, relying solely on multi-head self-attention, enabling parallel training and becoming the architecture of essentially all modern language models.

title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
authors: Bojanowski P, Grave E, Joulin A, Mikolov T
summary: fastText: represented words as bags of character n-grams, giving embeddings for rare and unseen words and morphologically rich languages.

title: A Distributional Perspective on Reinforcement Learning
authors: Bellemare MG, Dabney W, Munos R
summary: Learns the full distribution of returns instead of only its mean, introducing the categorical C51 algorithm. Distributional RL improved performance and opened a new line of research.

title: Curiosity-driven Exploration by Self-supervised Prediction
authors: Pathak D, Agrawal P, Efros AA, Darrell T
summary: The Intrinsic Curiosity Module rewards an agent for prediction errors of a forward model in a feature space learned by inverse dynamics, ignoring things the agent cannot control. It enabled exploration with sparse or no extrinsic reward.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
authors: Christiano PF, Leike J, Brown TB, Martic M, Legg S, Amodei D
subfield: RL from human feedback & for LLMs
summary: Learned a reward model from human comparisons of pairs of trajectory segments and optimized it with deep RL. It solved Atari and MuJoCo tasks with feedback on under 1% of interactions and is the basis of RLHF.

title: DeepStack: Expert-level artificial intelligence in heads-up no-limit poker
authors: Moravcik M, Schmid M, Burch N, Lisy V, Morrill D, Bard N, et al.
summary: Combined continual re-solving of subgames with deep value networks to beat professional players at heads-up no-limit Texas hold'em, a large imperfect-information game.

title: Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World
authors: Tobin J, Fong R, Ray A, Schneider J, Zaremba W, Abbeel P
summary: Randomizing textures, lighting and camera parameters in simulation makes the real world look like one more variation, so models trained only in simulation transfer to real robots. A key technique for sim-to-real transfer.

title: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge
authors: Silver D, Schrittwieser J, Simonyan K, Antonoglou I, Huang A, Guez A, et al.
summary: AlphaGo Zero learned Go purely from self-play with a single residual network trained to match MCTS-improved policies and game outcomes. Starting from random play, it surpassed every previous AlphaGo version.

title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments
authors: Lowe R, Wu Y, Tamar A, Harb J, Abbeel P, Mordatch I
summary: MADDPG trains centralized critics that see all agents' observations and actions alongside decentralized actors. This addresses non-stationarity in mixed cooperative-competitive settings.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
authors: Schulman J, Wolski F, Dhariwal P, Radford A, Klimov O
summary: PPO replaces TRPO's constrained optimization with a clipped surrogate objective that runs several epochs of minibatch updates. Simple and robust, it became the default RL algorithm, including for RLHF of language models.

title: Approval of Kymriah (tisagenlecleucel), the first CAR-T cell therapy
authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novartis
summary: First FDA-approved gene-modified cell therapy, for pediatric and young adult B-cell ALL.

title: Autologous induced stem-cell-derived retinal cells for macular degeneration
authors: Mandai M, Watanabe A, Kurimoto Y, Hirami Y, Morinaga C, Daimon T, et al.
summary: First transplantation of iPSC-derived tissue (retinal pigment epithelium) into a patient.

title: Efficacy and safety of voretigene neparvovec (AAV2-hRPE65v2) in patients with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy: a randomised, controlled, open-label, phase 3 trial
authors: Russell S, Bennett J, Wellman JA, Chung DC, Yu ZF, Tillman A, et al.
summary: Phase 3 trial supporting Luxturna, the first FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease (2017).

title: Immunogenicity and structures of a rationally designed prefusion MERS-CoV spike antigen
authors: Pallesen J, Wang N, Corbett KS, Wrapp D, Kirchdoerfer RN, Turner HL, et al.
summary: Introduced the two-proline (2P) prefusion-stabilizing mutations in coronavirus spikes, used in most COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Nusinersen versus sham control in infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy
authors: Finkel RS, Mercuri E, Darras BT, Connolly AM, Kuntz NL, Kirschner J, et al.
summary: ENDEAR trial of a splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide that increases SMN protein, the first approved SMA therapy.

title: Personalized RNA mutanome vaccines mobilize poly-specific therapeutic immunity against cancer
authors: Sahin U, Derhovanessian E, Miller M, Kloke BP, Simon P, Löwer M, et al.
summary: First-in-human individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccines in melanoma, establishing personalized cancer vaccines.

title: Single-dose gene-replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy
authors: Mendell JR, Al-Zaidy S, Shell R, Arnold WD, Rodino-Klapac LR, Prior TW, et al.
summary: Intravenous AAV9-SMN1 dramatically improved survival in SMA type 1 infants, leading to Zolgensma approval (2019).

title: Automatic chemical design using a data-driven continuous representation of molecules
authors: Gómez-Bombarelli R, Wei JN, Duvenaud D, Hernández-Lobato JM, Sánchez-Lengeling B, Sheberla D, et al.
summary: Used a variational autoencoder to map molecules to a continuous latent space for gradient-based generative molecular design.

title: Deep generative models of genetic variation capture the effects of mutations
authors: Riesselman AJ, Ingraham JB, Marks DS
summary: DeepSequence used VAEs on protein family alignments to predict mutation effects without labels.

title: SCANPY: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis
authors: Wolf FA, Angerer P, Theis FJ
summary: A scalable Python framework for single-cell analysis that anchors the scverse ecosystem.

title: Unsupervised Feature Learning via Non-Parametric Instance Discrimination
authors: Wu Z, Xiong Y, Yu SX, Lin D
summary: Instance discrimination with a memory bank and NCE loss, a direct precursor to MoCo and SimCLR.

title: Graph Attention Networks
authors: Veličković P, Cucurull G, Casanova A, Romero A, Liò P, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced attention-weighted neighborhood aggregation (GAT), letting GNNs learn the importance of neighbors.

title: JAX: Composable Transformations of Python+NumPy Programs
authors: Bradbury J, Frostig R, Hawkins P, Johnson MJ, Leary C, Maclaurin D, et al.
summary: Composable function transformations (grad, jit, vmap, pmap) compiled via XLA; widely used for large-scale research on TPUs and GPUs.

title: Mixed Precision Training
authors: Micikevicius P, Narang S, Alben J, Diamos G, Elsen E, Garcia D, et al.
summary: Trained networks in FP16 with FP32 master weights and loss scaling, halving memory and exploiting tensor cores.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Chen RTQ, Rubanova Y, Bettencourt J, Duvenaud D
summary: Treated network depth as continuous time, parameterizing hidden-state derivatives with a network and training via the adjoint method.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
authors: Jacot A, Gabriel F, Hongler C
summary: Showed infinitely wide networks trained by gradient descent behave as kernel regression with the neural tangent kernel.

title: Tensor Field Networks: Rotation- and Translation-Equivariant Neural Networks for 3D Point Clouds
authors: Thomas N, Smidt T, Kearnes S, Yang L, Li L, Kohlhoff K, et al.
summary: Built SE(3)-equivariant networks using spherical harmonics and tensor products, the basis of equivariant models for molecules.

title: Genome-wide polygenic scores for common diseases identify individuals with risk equivalent to monogenic mutations
authors: Khera AV, Chaffin M, Aragam KG, Haas ME, Roselli C, Choi SH, et al.
summary: Showed genome-wide polygenic scores identify individuals with risk comparable to monogenic mutations.

title: Genomic atlas of the human plasma proteome
authors: Sun BB, Maranville JC, Peters JE, Stacey D, Staley JR, Blackshaw J, et al.
summary: Mapped ~1,900 pQTLs for 3,600 plasma proteins measured by SomaScan, linking proteins to disease loci.

title: Highly parallel single-molecule identification of proteins in zeptomole-scale mixtures
authors: Swaminathan J, Boulgakov AA, Hernandez ET, Bardo AM, Bachman JL, Marotta J, et al.
summary: Fluorosequencing: single-molecule peptide identification by Edman degradation of fluorescently labelled residues.

title: Nanopore sequencing and assembly of a human genome with ultra-long reads
authors: Jain M, Koren S, Miga KH, Quick J, Rand AC, Sasani TA, et al.
summary: Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing of a human genome with reads exceeding 100 kb, demonstrating nanopore long reads for de novo assembly.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics of 20 mouse organs creates a Tabula Muris
authors: Tabula Muris Consortium
summary: Organism-wide mouse cell atlas from ~100,000 cells profiled with both droplet and Smart-seq2 methods.

title: The UK Biobank resource with deep phenotyping and genomic data
authors: Bycroft C, Freeman C, Petkova D, Band G, Elliott LT, Sharp K, et al.
summary: Genotypes and imputation for ~500,000 deeply phenotyped participants, powering biobank-scale genetics.

title: A CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive targeting doublesex causes complete population suppression in caged Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes
authors: Kyrou K, Hammond AM, Galizi R, Kranjc N, Burt A, Beaghton AK, et al.
summary: A drive targeting a conserved sex-determination gene collapsed caged malaria-mosquito populations without resistance arising, the strongest suppression-drive result to date.

title: De novo domestication of wild tomato using genome editing
authors: Zsögön A, Čermák T, Naves ER, Notini MM, Edel KH, Weinl S, et al.
summary: Edited a handful of known domestication genes in a wild tomato to recreate crop traits directly, proposing de novo domestication as a breeding strategy.

title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
authors: Peters ME, Neumann M, Iyyer M, Gardner M, Clark C, Lee K, Zettlemoyer L
summary: ELMo: contextual word representations from a deep bidirectional LSTM language model, delivering large gains across NLP tasks and heralding pretraining.

title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
authors: Radford A, Narasimhan K, Salimans T, Sutskever I
summary: GPT-1: generative pretraining of a Transformer decoder followed by discriminative fine-tuning, establishing the pretrain-then-fine-tune Transformer recipe.

title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
authors: Howard J, Ruder S
summary: ULMFiT showed that pretraining an LSTM language model and fine-tuning it with careful schedules transfers strongly to text classification.

title: A general reinforcement learning algorithm that masters chess, shogi, and Go through self-play
authors: Silver D, Hubert T, Schrittwieser J, Antonoglou I, Lai M, Guez A, et al.
summary: AlphaZero applied the AlphaGo Zero algorithm, with no domain knowledge beyond the rules, to chess, shogi and Go, and beat world-champion programs in all three. It showed that one self-play method can generalize across games.

title: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods
authors: Fujimoto S, van Hoof H, Meger D
summary: TD3 addresses overestimation in DDPG with clipped double-Q learning, delayed policy updates and target policy smoothing. It became a strong standard baseline for continuous control.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Handful of Trials using Probabilistic Dynamics Models
authors: Chua K, Calandra R, McAllister R, Levine S
summary: PETS uses ensembles of probabilistic neural network dynamics models with trajectory sampling for model-predictive control. It matched model-free asymptotic performance with far fewer samples.

title: IMPALA: Scalable Distributed Deep-RL with Importance Weighted Actor-Learner Architectures
